source_rows.title: launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for Driving Schools Monitoring and Test Management project through Public-Private Partnership (PPP)

raw.title: launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for Driving Schools Monitoring and Test Management project through Public-Private Partnership (PPP)
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 28/07/2024 Previous Next launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for Driving Schools Monitoring and Test Management project through Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Page Image Riyadh, July 2024: The Ministry of interior (MOI), in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) Page Content Riyadh, July 2024: The Ministry of interior (MOI), in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for Driving Schools Monitoring and Test Management project through Public-Private Partnership (PPP). This project aims to monitor the performance of driving schools and administer driving tests in the Kingdom, with the key objective of enhancing the quality and efficiency of driving tests and raise the standards of driving schools. There are currently more than 69 driving schools throughout the Kingdom. The project will be tendered under an operation and management (O&M) model, with a contract duration of 10 years, including 18 months for the project implementation. The project involves both driving test management and driving school monitoring. It includes operating and managing driving tests, which encompasses, pre-evaluation, theoretical, and practical tests, arranging necessary equipment, preparing tests based on the General Department of Traffic guidelines, and training testing staff, including examiners and assessors. Additionally, it involves developing standards for evaluating driving schools and trainers, conducting on-site evaluations, monitoring performance and compliance with key performance indicators (KPIs). It includes developing action plans for driving schools' improvement and submission of reports to the Ministry of interior and the General department of Traffic. Ministry of Interior and National Center for Privatization & PPP invited local and international investors interested in the project to visit the NCP website and review the EOI document. All interested companies should submit their EOI by 25 August 2024 at 3:00pm KSA time. Share | Print

raw.title: Saudi Broadcasting Authority, National Center for Privatization & PPP Launch Expression of Interest Phase for Television & Radio Towers Infrastructure PPP Project in 143 Locations
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 06/09/2024 Previous Next Saudi Broadcasting Authority, National Center for Privatization & PPP Launch Expression of Interest Phase for Television & Radio Towers Infrastructure PPP Project in 143 Locations Page Image ​​The Saudi Broadcasting Authority (SBA), in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) Page Content ​​ The Saudi Broadcasting Authority (SBA), in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for the Television & Radio Towers Infrastructure PPP project to develop and operate the SBA towers infrastructure by the private sector under a Rehabilitate-Finance-Operate-Maintain-Transfer (RFOMT) contract model with a 25 years contract. The project is considered one of the Public-Private-Partnership (PPP) projects aimed to enhance the performance of the TV and radio towers infrastructure for the media sector in the Kingdom at 143 locations and increasing the number of TV and radio channels by qualifying and upgrading all TV sites from (DVB-T/Analogue) to (DVB-T2), with the aim of increasing the number of high-quality channels, and maintaining and operating the TV and radio towers infrastructure. SBA and NCP invited investors and interested parties to review the EOI document - containing project information - by visiting the NCP website, ( www.ncp.gov.sa ), noting that the EOI submission phase will end on 21 July, 2024, at 3:00 PM KSA time. source_rows.title: NCEC in Collaboration with MEWA and NCP Launches EOI for Environmental Inspection Project

raw.title: NCEC in Collaboration with MEWA and NCP Launches EOI for Environmental Inspection Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 17/09/2025 Previous Next NCEC in Collaboration with MEWA and NCP Launches EOI for Environmental Inspection Project Page Image The project marks a significant step toward enhancing environmental compliance and regulatory enforcement in the Kingdom. Page Content ​​​ Riyadh, September 2025 – The National Center for Environmental Compliance (NCEC), in collaboration with the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (MEWA) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for the Environmental Inspection Project. This project will be executed under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model through a 10-year Operation and Management (O&M) contract. This project marks a significant step toward enhancing environmental compliance and regulatory enforcement in the Kingdom. The private sector partner will be responsible for conducting nationwide environmental inspections, ensuring adherence to regulatory standards at approximately 250,000 facilities across the Kingdom. The project scope includes recruiting and training inspectors, providing, maintaining, and operating all necessary vehicles and equipment. Additionally, the inspection process will be digitalized through the development of an advanced electronic system to document inspection visits, ensuring seamless data transfer and generating comprehensive post-visit reports. The project aims to expand inspection coverage, improve operational efficiency and quality standards, as well as streamline compliance procedures reinforcing Saudi Arabia's commitment to international environmental standards. It also aligns with the goals of Vision 2030, supporting sustainability efforts and accelerating the digital transformation of environmental monitoring. Local and international investors are invited to visit the NCEC website at ( www.ncec.gov.sa ) for more information about the project and to request the EOI document. Interested investors should submit their EOI by 6 October, 2025 at 11:59 pm KSA time. ​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: MIC in Collaboration with the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources and NCP Announces Privatization of the Military Uniform and Accessories Factory

raw.title: MIC in Collaboration with the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources and NCP Announces Privatization of the Military Uniform and Accessories Factory
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 18/09/2025 Previous Next MIC in Collaboration with the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources and NCP Announces Privatization of the Military Uniform and Accessories Factory Page Image It will also sustain and enhance production capacity for military and non-military uniforms and accessories, while enabling the development of new business opportunities, including entry into B2B markets and export growth Page Content ​​​ Riyadh, September 2025 , The Military Industries Corporation (MIC), in collaboration with the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources (MIM) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for the privatization of the Military Uniform and Accessories Factory (MUAF) project in Riyadh and Al Kharj. The privatization will be executed through a purchase agreement, transferring full ownership of MUAF from MIC to the private sector. The transfer of ownership will ensure compliance with military industry regulations and licensing requirements set by the General Authority for Military Industries (GAMI). It will also sustain and enhance production capacity for military and non-military uniforms and accessories, while enabling the development of new business opportunities, including entry into B2B markets and export growth. In addition, the process will support a smooth transition of operations, workforce, and supply chain management under private ownership. This step highlights the Kingdom's commitment to building a competitive, sustainable, and innovative defense industry ecosystem, while strengthening the overall industrial base. It also creates new opportunities for private sector participation across strategic sectors in line with the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030. Local and international investors are invited to visit the NCP website at www.ncp.gov.sa to review further information and details of the EOI and RFQ. The deadline for submitting SOQ is 16 October 2025, at 03:00 PM (KSA time).​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: Umm Al-Qura University, and NCP Announce Launch of EOI Phase for the Completion and Operation of Umm Al-Qura University Hospital PPP Project
source_rows.owner: Qura University Hospital PPP Project Page Image PPP project to complete

raw.title: Umm Al-Qura University, and NCP Announce Launch of EOI Phase for the Completion and Operation of Umm Al-Qura University Hospital PPP Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 30/06/2026 Previous Next Umm Al-Qura University, and NCP Announce Launch of EOI Phase for the Completion and Operation of Umm Al-Qura University Hospital PPP Project Page Image PPP project to complete and operate a 391-bed university hospital, delivering high-quality specialized and secondary healthcare services while supporting medical education, training, and research Page Content Riyadh, June 2026: Umm Al-Qura University, and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) announced the launch of the Expressions of Interest (EOI) phase for the completion and operation of Umm Al-Qura University Hospital in the Makkah Region, under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model through a Design, Build, Finance, Operate, and Maintain (DBFOM) contract for a period of 30 years. The Project aims to revitalize a strategic state asset by activating an existing hospital and transforming it into a fully integrated university hospital operating at full capacity, with a total capacity of 391 beds. The scope of the Project includes the rehabilitation and completion of the remaining construction works for the hospital, in addition to its full operation through the delivery of integrated clinical and healthcare services, including inpatient, outpatient, emergency, surgical, and diagnostic services, along with the provision of core medical specialties and the management of facilities and supporting medical services. The Umm Al-Qura University Hospital Project supports medical education, training, and scientific research for national talent, alongside the delivery of high-quality specialized and secondary healthcare services to the population of the region. The Project is centered on enhancing the optimal use of state assets and achieving financial sustainability in line with Saudi Vision 2030, by enabling the private sector to equip and operate the assets to improve the efficiency of government spending, manage human capital, and ensure integration with the University's medical education and training programs in line with market needs and international best practices. Local and international investors, financial institutions, and operators are invited to visit the NCP website at investors​.ncp.gov.sa for more information about the project and to request the EOI document. Interested investors should submit their EOI by July 21, 2026 at 11:59 PM KSA time. ​ Share | Print

raw.title: YANBU NON-HAZARDOUS INDUSTRIAL WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY
raw.description:
The project aims to establish a treatment facility for non-hazardous industrial waste across Yanbu cluster.

The global industrial waste management market was valued at 
USD 791.14B in 2020. It is estimated to expand at a CAGR of 
10.4% from 2021 to 2031 

The global industrial waste management market is expected 
to cross the value of USD 2.3 T by the end of 2031

Industrial waste constitutes approximately half of the share of 
the overall waste generated across the globe

The operation would require a continuous input of non-
hazardous industrial waste from private waste collectors
The historic and projected growth in industrial 
sector as part of the KSA transformation requires 
innovative solutions for treatment of industrial 
waste
The drive to increase private sector participation 
and competitiveness in the economy are further 
drivers for formulation of the opportunity
The need to modernize waste management sector 
in the Kingdom is a key driver to attracting 
investors and operators 
* CAGR
M USD 

As KSA continues to expand the industrial sector as part of 
Vision 2030 the project enables the industrial waste operator 
to capitalize on a growing segment on Saudi Arabia's 
economy

The opportunity allows a potential investor to deliver a 
greenfield project with no constraints from legacy 
infrastructure in a developing sector enabling a full use of 
best-in-class operational and technical solutions



Plant capacity: 46,000 tons of waste per year


source_rows.title: HAFAR ALBATIN INERT LANDFILL

raw.title: HAFAR ALBATIN INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Hafar Al Batin.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Hafar Al Batin’s population growth and expansion 
are the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 1.7M USD*

Plant capacity: 282,585 tons

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 28M USD


source_rows.title: YANBU CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 1

raw.title: YANBU CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 1
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Yanbu
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Yanbu's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the 
development of the infrastructure sector, which is 
expected to lead to an increase in waste 
generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD

Location (Region): Yanbu

source_rows.title: ALBAHA HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER

raw.title: ALBAHA HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER
raw.description:
The opportunity aims to operate a healthcare waste treatment infrastructure across all AlBaha cluster.

Driven by the Covid-19 health crisis, medical waste has increased to 2.6 
M tons per day worldwide

Healthcare waste management market globally had a revenue of USD 
12.8 bn in 2021. It is expected to be growing at a CAGR of 6.9% during 
the forecast period (2022-2030)

Market dynamics are also driven by the increasing use of reusable 
surgical products and rising awareness programs for medical waste 
management in developed countries

The project would require healthcare waste provided from 
public and private healthcare providers and transported to the 
facilities through waste collection and transfer operators in 
AlBaha Cluster

Expansion and modernization of the healthcare sector are 
increasing the demand for healthcare waste management 
services

Growth in economic and population in KSA and further 
expansion of AlBaha are additional demand drivers and 
are projected to increase in the future

Drive to increase public sector participation and 
competitiveness in the economy are further drivers for 
formulation of the opportunity
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 3M USD*

Plant capacity: 2,156 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 8.43 years

GDP Impact: 35M USD

Location (Region): AlBaha Cluster

AlBaha’s population is expected to continue to grow over the next few 
decades, which can potentially generate significant demand for the 
project

The investment opportunity focusses on creating waste treatment 
infrastructure, which provides a level of assurance while also offering 
attractive returns to potential investors

raw.title: AL QASSIM INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Al Qassim.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Al Qassim's population growth and expansion are 
the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions

source_rows.title: MoS in Collaboration with NCP and Riyadh Region Municipality Launch EOI and RFQ for Prince Faisal bin Fahad Sports City Project

raw.title: MoS in Collaboration with NCP and Riyadh Region Municipality Launch EOI and RFQ for Prince Faisal bin Fahad Sports City Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 14/08/2025 Previous Next MoS in Collaboration with NCP and Riyadh Region Municipality Launch EOI and RFQ for Prince Faisal bin Fahad Sports City Project Page Image This new stadium will feature a seating capacity of approximately 47,000 spectators. Once completed, it is expected to host major domestic and international football events, including the 2034 FIFA World Cup. Page Content ​ MoS in Collaboration with NCP and Riyadh Region Municipality Launch EOI and RFQ for Prince Faisal bin Fahad Sports City Project Riyadh, August 2025 – The Ministry of Sport (MoS), in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) and Riyadh Region Municipality, is pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for the Prince Faisal bin Fahad Sports (PFBF) Sports City. This Public-Private Partnership (PPP) project will be delivered under a Design, Build, Finance, Operate, Maintain (DBFOM) model with a (20 – 30) year contract term. PFBF Sports City project presents an opportunity to develop a stadium north of King Abdullah Park in Al-Malaz, adjacent to the current facility. This new stadium will feature a seating capacity of approximately 47,000 spectators. Once completed, it is expected to host major domestic and international football events, including the 2034 FIFA World Cup. The project also includes developing the plan for PFBF Sports City, including the existing stadium. The project reflects the successful cooperation between the public sector, represented by MoS, NCP, and Riyadh Region Municipality. It also strengthens the distinguished partnership between government entities and the private sector by developing PFBF Sports City and preparing it to host major sporting and diverse cultural events, while ensuring commercial sustainability and increasing revenues. This aligns with joint efforts to drive economic growth and achieve national aspirations. ​ MoS and NCP invite interested local and international investors to visit the NCP website at investors.ncp.gov.sa for more information about the project and to request the RFQ document. Interested investors should submit their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) by October 13, 2025 at 3:00 PM, KSA time. Share | Print

source_rows.title: MOMAH and NCP Launch EOI to Municipal Food Safety Labs Across Five Municipalities in Saudi Arabia
source_rows.raw_location: Al-Ahsa, Tabuk, Qassim, Hafr Al Batin, Northern Borders

raw.title: MOMAH and NCP Launch EOI to Municipal Food Safety Labs Across Five Municipalities in Saudi Arabia
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 01/04/2026 Previous Next MOMAH and NCP Launch EOI to Municipal Food Safety Labs Across Five Municipalities in Saudi Arabia Page Image Developing advanced food safety labs to enhance testing, ensure quality, and protect public health in line with Vision 2030. Page Content Riyadh, April 2026 , the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing (MOMAH) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), have announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) stage for the Municipal Food Safety Labs Operation Project under a PPP framework (Equip-Operate-Maintain-Transfer) for a contract duration of 5 years, inviting local, regional, and global companies with experience in lab operations to participate and submit their bids. The project scope includes equipping, operating, and maintaining food safety labs across five municipalities, including Hafr Al Batin, Northern Borders, Tabuk, Qassim, and Al Ahsa. The project aims to upgrade lab equipment, expand chemical and microbiological testing capacity for food and water products, ensure testing accuracy to support the lab compliance value chain, and facilitate ongoing knowledge transfer and end-of-contract handover to the respective municipalities. The Municipal Food Safety Labs Operation Project seeks to boost public health and safety standards for the Kingdom's citizens and residents in line with the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030, besides developing the municipal monitoring ecosystem, optimizing food and water testing, and empowering the private sector to run operations as per global best practices. Once completed, the project will enhance food safety in the Kingdom, enable sustainable growth across targeted regions by creating unique investment opportunities for the private sector, and improve the efficiency of government spending through the PPP model, playing a key role in elevating the quality of municipal services being offered to citizens and residents. Local and international investors, financial institutions, and operators are invited to visit the NCP website at www.investors.ncp​.gov.sa for more information about the project and to request the EOI document. Interested investors should submit their EOI by 15 April 2026 at 11:59 PM KSA time.​ ​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: Following the approval of a project document by the Council of Ministers offering 14 sports clubs for privatization
source_rows.owner: the Ministry's enthusiasm to be able to help sports teams become financially sustainable

raw.title: Following the approval of a project document by the Council of Ministers offering 14 sports clubs for privatization
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 12/06/2024 Previous Next Following the approval of a project document by the Council of Ministers offering 14 sports clubs for privatization Page Image Following the approval of a project document by the Council of Ministers offering 14 sports clubs for privatization Page Content MOS in collaboration with NCP, Announces the Start of Second Phase of Sports Clubs Investment and Privatization Project Second Track​​​ Ministry of Sport announced today Wednesday, 3 July 2024, in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), the start of the second phase of the second track in the Sports Clubs Investment and Privatization Project. This occurred subsequent to the Council of Ministers' resolution, which was made on Tuesday, July 2, 2024, to approve the project document for the privatization of 14 teams from various divisions. This also came to continue the project launched by HRH the Crown Prince back in June of last year. The project aims to attain the objectives of the Kingdom's Vision 2030 and to encourage the business sector to take part in the establishment and growth of the sports industry in a manner that would benefit all teams, clubs, players, and fans. In the second phase of the second track, sports clubs at various levels will be made available for privatization to both domestic and foreign investors. The first batch of clubs included six clubs (Al-Zulfi, Al-Nahda, Al-Okhdood, Al-Ansar, Al-Orouba, and Al-Kholoud). Investors can visit the investor portal on the NCP website to apply and get the required information if they would want to invest in the clubs included in the first batch starting from August 2024. Al-Shoulla, Hajar, Al-Najma, Al-Riyadh, Al-Rawda, Jeddah, Al-Taraji, and Al-Sahel are the next eight clubs whose offerings will be completed sequentially later. There were two primary tracks used to initiate the project. The first was granting permission for businesses and development organizations to invest in sports teams in return for a transfer of ownership. There were eight clubs on this track. The second track, which was launched, offered several sports clubs for privatization. The track will now be completed with a second phase, which is offering six clubs for privatization, with the stage being completed by offering other clubs during the coming period, in accordance with the project's strategic plans. The first phase of the track involved registering the interest of local and international entities wishing to invest in sports clubs. This announcement is in line with the efforts made to accomplish the main goals of the club investment and privatization project, which include improving the administrative and financial governance of sports clubs, creating an environment that is conducive to sports investment, and improving the fan experience through the development of infrastructure. The project also demonstrates the Ministry's enthusiasm to be able to help sports teams become financially sustainable and operate at the highest levels of professionalism and try to solidify its relationships with businesses.​​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: Following Completion of the Privatization Program  Minister of Finance Announces Launch of the National Privatization Strategy ​

raw.title: Following Completion of the Privatization Program  Minister of Finance Announces Launch of the National Privatization Strategy ​
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 29/01/2026 Previous Next Following Completion of the Privatization Program Minister of Finance Announces Launch of the National Privatization Strategy ​ Page Image The National Privatization Strategy aims to increase satisfaction with services provided to citizens, residents, and visitors across 18 targeted sectors through the creation of tens of thousands of high-quality jobs. Page Content ​ His Excellency Mohammed bin Abdullah al-Jadaan, the Minister of Finance and Chairman of the Board of Directors of the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), has declared that the Council of Economic and Development Affairs (CEDA) has granted approval to finalize the Privatization Program, following the successful execution of its projects and initiatives as per the established plan. His Excellency noted that since its launch, the Privatization Program achieved several accomplishments, most notably the establishment of NCP, which developed more than 200 approved projects with total investments reaching $213 billion. The program also oversaw the signing of nearly 90 contracts, including asset transfer and public-private partnership (PPP) agreements across several sectors. In addition, it contributed to strengthening the role of the private sector, improving the operational efficiency of government assets, and developing the legislative and regulatory environment supportive of investment, thereby supporting economic diversification and enhancing the Kingdom's competitiveness. The Minister of Finance also praised the approval of the National Privatization Strategy by the Council of Ministers on 25 November 2025. He announced the commencement of the implementation of the National Privatization Strategy, which aims to enhance the quality and efficiency of infrastructure and advance the public services provided to the Kingdom's population. The strategy also seeks to strengthen the role of the private sector in sustainable economic development, enable the government to focus on its legislative, supervisory, and regulatory roles, and enhance fiscal sustainability, in line with the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030. His Excellency stated: “ In the Kingdom, we strive to establish future-ready infrastructure with high quality and efficiency, ensuring that public services delivered to citizens, residents, and visitors are among the best in the world, while strengthening the Kingdom's position as a global reference in public-private partnerships ." The National Privatization Strategy aims to increase satisfaction with services provided to citizens, residents, and visitors across 18 targeted sectors through the creation of tens of thousands of high-quality jobs. It also targets signing more than 220 public-private partnership contracts by 2030 and increasing private-sector capital investments to more than $64 billion by 2030. The strategy has outlined five main programs to enable and advance the privatization ecosystem, along with 42 executive initiatives to achieve its objectives and the privatization-related targets of Saudi Vision 2030. It also includes an executive program focused on identifying and prioritizing privatization opportunities, through which more than 145 priority opportunities have been identified, representing attractive investment prospects for the private sector. The launch of the National Privatization Strategy marks the conclusion of the Privatization Program in accordance with the plan set at its inception in 2018, and the transition from the foundational phase, successfully completed by the program, to the implementation phase and acceleration of delivery, as the Privatization Program has fulfilled the core purpose for which it was established. raw.title: MAKKAH INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Makkah.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Makkah's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions

market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Makkah's population growth and expansion are the main 
drivers of construction and demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development of the 
infrastructure sector, which is expected to lead to an 
increase in waste generation necessitating further waste 
management solutions

the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

source_rows.title: Saudi Arabia Launches EOI and RFQ Phase for Chronic Kidney Disease Care & National Dialysis Services

raw.title: Saudi Arabia Launches EOI and RFQ Phase for Chronic Kidney Disease Care & National Dialysis Services
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 04/05/2026 Previous Next Saudi Arabia Launches EOI and RFQ Phase for Chronic Kidney Disease Care & National Dialysis Services Page Image A PPP project to provide renal care services to over 11,500 patients across the Kingdom ensuring broad geographic coverage. Page Content ​ Riyadh, May 2026 : The Ministry of Health (MoH), the Ministry of Defense (MoD) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) have announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for the Chronic Kidney Disease Care & National Dialysis Services project. The project will be executed under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model Design, Repurpose, Finance and Maintain (DRFM), with a 6-year contract, in addition to a clinical services model. The project aligns with a key objective of Saudi Vision 2030 by promoting increased private sector participation within the healthcare sector. The MoH is seeking to partner with experienced private operators to deliver comprehensive renal care services to a minimum of 11,500 patients throughout the Kingdom. The project is divided across 4 packages, each serving a minimum number of patients across several regions, to ensure broad geographic coverage and accessibility. Details about the size and geographical coverage of each Package will be provided at the RFP stage. Under this PPP framework, the MoH and the selected private operator for each package will have an agreement, outlining the terms of collaboration. The selected Private Operators will be responsible for providing the necessary facilities, equipment, and IT services. They must also supply qualified staff, manage both clinical (In-center hemodialysis, home hemodialysis, Peritoneal dialysis, vascular access and OPD services) and non-clinical operations. Local and international investors, financial institutions, and operators are invited to visit the NCP website at investors.ncp.gov.sa for more information about the project and to request the RFQ document. Interested investors should submit their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) by June 15, 2026 at 15:00 PM, KSA time.​ Share | Print

raw.title: The Ministry of health and the National Center for Privatization & PPP Announce Award of SABIC Behavioral Health Hospital PPP Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 18/06/2026 Previous Next The Ministry of health and the National Center for Privatization & PPP Announce Award of SABIC Behavioral Health Hospital PPP Project Page Image The project comes within the objectives of the Health Sector Transformation Program, which aims to improve the quality and efficiency of health services, and enhance the participation of the private sector in providing quality and specialized services Page Content ​​​​ The Ministry of Health and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) announced the award of the operation and management contract for the SABIC Specialized Behavioral Healthcare Hospital to a SEH Healthcare as part of the Privatization and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models. The project comes within the objectives of the Health Sector Transformation Program, which aims to improve the quality and efficiency of health services, and enhance the participation of the private sector in providing quality and specialized services, which contributes to increasing capacity, improving the beneficiary experience, and facilitating access to mental health and behavioral care services. The project represents an extension of the integrated cooperation between the Ministry of Health and SABIC, which contributed to the construction, equipping and developing the hospital building and its infrastructure, on a total area of 62,500 square meters, with a capacity of up to 150 beds, which enhances the ability of the health system to provide specialized and integrated services in the fields of mental health and behavioral care. SEH Healthcare formed by SMC Healthcare, which operates hospitals and specialized medical centers in Riyadh, the German “Dr. Ebel" group, which specializes in rehabilitation, treatment, psychological and rehabilitative care services, and “Health Gates Complex," which specializes in mental health care.​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: YANBU END OF LIFE TYRES TREATMENT FACILITY

raw.title: YANBU END OF LIFE TYRES TREATMENT FACILITY
raw.description:
The aim of this opportunity is to create a waste tire treatment facility for the entire Yanbu cluster.

Nearly one billion ELTs are generated worldwide annually, 
constituting more than 2% of the total amount of solid waste, and 
this waste flow is growing dynamically

The operation would require a stable input of end-of-life tires 
from producers for processing the waste

The rise in personal wealth and transforming 
consumer behavior in the Kingdom (increasing 
digitization, increasing personal consumption etc.) 
are increasing tire consumption requiring uplift in 
waste treatment solutions 

Waste management sector transformation driven by 
the Vision 2030 and initiatives to increase private 
sector participation require innovative, and 
sustainable solutions in KSA

The high level of economic and population growth in the KSA is 
expected to generate significant increase in consumption over the 
coming years, thus creating an opportunity for an end-of-life tire 
treatment facility operator to enter an attractive market

The Kingdom is placing a significant focus on the waste 
management sector as part of the Vision 2030 and the project 
can expect high level of engagement from the relevant authorities 
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 1M USD*

Plant capacity: 2,500 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 7.96 years

GDP Impact: 19M USD

Location (Region): Yanbu Cluster

source_rows.title: AL QUNFUDHAH HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER

raw.title: AL QUNFUDHAH HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER
raw.description:
The opportunity aims to operate a healthcare waste treatment infrastructure across all Al Qunfudhah cluster.

Driven by the Covid-19 health crisis, medical waste has 
increased to 2.6 M tons per day worldwide

Healthcare waste management market globally had a revenue 
of USD 12.8 bn in 2021. It is expected to be growing at a 
CAGR of 6.9% during the forecast period (2022-2030)

Market dynamics are also driven by the increasing use of 
reusable surgical products and rising awareness programs for 
medical waste management in developed countries

The project would require healthcare waste provided 
from public and private healthcare providers and 
transported to the facilities through waste collection 
and transfer operators in Al Qunfudhah Cluster

Expansion and modernization of the healthcare 
sector are increasing the demand for healthcare 
waste management services

Growth in economic and population in KSA and 
further expansion of Al Qunfudhah are additional 
demand drivers and are projected to increase in 
the future

Drive to increase public sector participation and 
competitiveness in the economy are further drivers 
for formulation of the opportunity
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 0.5M USD*

Plant capacity: 1,300 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 6.84 years

GDP Impact: 23M USD

Location (Region): Al Qunfudhah Cluster

Al Qunfudhah’s population is expected to continue to grow 
over the next few decades, which can potentially generate 
significant demand for the project

The investment opportunity focusses on creating waste 
treatment infrastructure, which provides a level of assurance 
while also offering attractive returns to potential investors

source_rows.title: Dammam END OF LIFE TYRES TREATMENT FACILITY 1

raw.title: Dammam END OF LIFE TYRES TREATMENT FACILITY 1
raw.description:
The aim of this opportunity is to create a waste tire treatment facility for the entire Dammam Cluster.

Nearly one billion ELTs are generated worldwide annually, constituting 
more than 2% of the total amount of solid waste, and this waste flow is 
growing dynamically

The operation would require a stable input of end-of-life tires from 
producers for processing and transfer along the further waste treatment 
value chain

The rise in personal wealth and transforming consumer 
behavior in the Kingdom (increasing digitization, increasing 
personal consumption etc.) are increasing tire 
consumption requiring uplift in waste treatment solutions 


source_rows.title: AL QUNFUDHAH INERT LANDFILL

raw.title: AL QUNFUDHAH INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Al Qunfudhah.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.

Al Qunfudhah's population growth and expansion 
are the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 2.2M USD*

Plant capacity: 374,838 tons 

Expected IRR: 10.33%

Payback period: 6.54 years

GDP Impact: 37M USD


source_rows.title: AL QUNFUDHAH CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2

raw.title: AL QUNFUDHAH CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 2
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Al Qunfudhah
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Al Qunfudhah's population growth and expansion 
are the main drivers of construction and demolition 
waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.53M USD*

Plant capacity: 300,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 95M USD


raw.title: YANBU HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER
raw.description:
The opportunity aims to operate a healthcare waste treatment infrastructure across all Yanbu cluster.

Driven by the Covid-19 health crisis, medical waste has 
increased to 2.6 M tons per day worldwide

Healthcare waste management market globally had a revenue 
of USD 12.8 bn in 2021. It is expected to be growing at a 
CAGR of 6.9% during the forecast period (2022-2030)

Market dynamics are also driven by the increasing use of 
reusable surgical products and rising awareness programs for 
medical waste management in developed countries

The project would require healthcare waste provided 
from public and private healthcare providers and 
transported to the facilities through waste collection 
and transfer operators in Yanbu Cluster

Expansion and modernization of the healthcare 
sector are increasing the demand for healthcare 
waste management services

Growth in economic and population in KSA and 
further expansion of Yanbu are additional demand 
drivers and are projected to increase in the future

Drive to increase public sector participation and 
competitiveness in the economy are further drivers 
for formulation of the opportunity
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 1M USD*

Plant capacity: 1,500 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 6.83 years

GDP Impact: 24M USD

Location (Region): Yanbu Cluster

Yanbu’s population is expected to continue to grow over the 
next few decades, which can potentially generate significant 
demand for the project

The investment opportunity focusses on creating waste 
treatment infrastructure, which provides a level of assurance 
while also offering attractive returns to potential investors

raw.title: TABUK END OF LIFE TYRES TREATMENT
raw.description:
The aim of this opportunity is to create a waste tire treatment facility for the entire Tabuk cluster.

Nearly one billion ELTs are generated worldwide annually, 
constituting more than 2% of the total amount of solid waste, 
and this waste flow is growing dynamically

The operation would require a stable input of end-of-life tires 
from producers for processing the waste

The rise in personal wealth and transforming 
consumer behavior in the Kingdom (increasing 
digitization, increasing personal consumption etc.) 
are increasing tire consumption requiring uplift in 
waste treatment solutions 

Waste management sector transformation driven 
by the Vision 2030 and initiatives to increase 
private sector participation require innovative, and 
sustainable solutions in KSA

The high level of economic and population growth in the KSA 
is expected to generate significant increase in consumption 
over the coming years, thus creating an opportunity for an 
end-of-life tire treatment facility operator to enter an attractive 
market

The Kingdom is placing a significant focus on the waste 
management sector as part of the Vision 2030 and the project 
can expect high level of engagement from the relevant 
authorities 
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 0.6M USD*

Plant capacity: 3,800 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 16.09%

Payback period: 5.32 years

GDP Impact: 18M USD

Location (Region): Tabuk Cluster

raw.title: TAIF HAZARDOUS INDUSTRIAL WASTE TREATMENT
raw.description:
The project aims to establish a treatment center mainly for hazardous industrial waste across Taif cluster.

The global industrial waste management market was valued at 
USD 791.14B in 2020. It is estimated to expand at a CAGR of 
10.4% from 2021 to 2031 

The global industrial waste management market is expected to 
cross the value of USD 2.3 T by the end of 2031

Industrial waste constitutes approximately half of the share of the 
overall waste generated across the globe

The operation would mainly require a continuous input of 
hazardous industrial waste from private waste collectors. This 
opportunity also receives waste from other streams such as 
agricultural, healthcare and ELV waste.
The historic and projected growth in industrial 
sector as part of the KSA transformation 
requires innovative solutions for treatment of 
hazardous industrial waste
The drive to increase private sector 
participation and competitiveness in the 
economy are further drivers for formulation of 
the opportunity
The need to modernize waste management 
sector in the Kingdom is a key driver to 
attracting investors and operators 
* CAGR
M USD 

As KSA continues to expand the industrial sector as part of Vision 
2030 the project enables a hazardous industrial waste operator to 
capitalize on a growing segment on Saudi Arabia's economy

The opportunity allows a potential investor to deliver a greenfield 
project with no constraints from legacy infrastructure in a 
developing sector enabling a full use of best-in-class operational 
and technical solutions

Expected Investment size: 26M USD*

Plant capacity: 21,241 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 7.67 years

GDP Impact: 138M USD

Location (Region): Taif Cluster


Nearly one billion ELTs are generated worldwide annually, 
constituting more than 2% of the total amount of solid waste, 
and this waste flow is growing dynamically


from producers for processing the waste

The rise in personal wealth and transforming 
consumer behavior in the Kingdom (increasing 
digitization, increasing personal consumption 
etc.) are increasing tire consumption requiring 
uplift in waste treatment solutions 

Waste management sector transformation 
driven by the Vision 2030 and initiatives to 
increase private sector participation require 
innovative, and sustainable solutions in KSA

The high level of economic and population growth in the KSA

over the coming years, thus creating an opportunity for an 
end-of-life tire treatment facility operator to enter an attractive 
market

authorities

hazardous industrial waste from private waste collectors.

such as agricultural, healthcare and ELV waste.

sector as part of the KSA transformation requires 
innovative solutions for treatment of hazardous 
industrial waste

drivers for formulation of the opportunity

in the Kingdom is a key driver to attracting 
investors and operators

economy

raw.title: NAJRAN HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER
raw.description:
The opportunity aims to operate a healthcare waste treatment infrastructure across all Najran cluster.

Driven by the Covid-19 health crisis, medical waste has 
increased to 2.6 M tons per day worldwide

Healthcare waste management market globally had a revenue 
of USD 12.8 bn in 2021. It is expected to be growing at a 
CAGR of 6.9% during the forecast period (2022-2030)

Market dynamics are also driven by the increasing use of 
reusable surgical products and rising awareness programs for 
medical waste management in developed countries

The project would require healthcare waste provided 
from public and private healthcare providers and 
transported to the facilities through waste collection 
and transfer operators in Najran Cluster

Expansion and modernization of the healthcare 
sector are increasing the demand for healthcare 
waste management services

Growth in economic and population in KSA and 
further expansion of Najran are additional 
demand drivers and are projected to increase in 
the future

Drive to increase public sector participation and 
competitiveness in the economy are further 
drivers for formulation of the opportunity
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 1M USD*

Plant capacity: 1,200 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 6.82 years

GDP Impact: 20M USD

Location (Region): Najran Cluster

Najran’s population is expected to continue to grow over the 
next few decades, which can potentially generate significant 
demand for the project

The investment opportunity focusses on creating waste 
treatment infrastructure, which provides a level of assurance 
while also offering attractive returns to potential investors

source_rows.title: NORTHERN BORDERS HAZARDOUS INDUSTRIAL WASTE TREATMENT

raw.title: NORTHERN BORDERS HAZARDOUS INDUSTRIAL WASTE TREATMENT
raw.description:
The project aims to establish a treatment center mainly for hazardous industrial waste across Northern Borders cluster.

The global industrial waste management market was valued at 
USD 791.14B in 2020. It is estimated to expand at a CAGR of 
10.4% from 2021 to 2031 

The global industrial waste management market is expected 
to cross the value of USD 2.3 T by the end of 2031

Industrial waste constitutes approximately half of the share of 
the overall waste generated across the globe

The operation would mainly require a continuous input of 
hazardous industrial waste from private waste collectors. 
This opportunity also receives waste from other streams 
such as agricultural, healthcare and ELV waste.
The historic and projected growth in industrial sector 
as part of the KSA transformation requires innovative 
solutions for treatment of hazardous industrial waste
The drive to increase private sector participation and 
competitiveness in the economy are further drivers for 
formulation of the opportunity
The need to modernize waste management sector in 
the Kingdom is a key driver to attracting investors and 
operators 
* CAGR
M USD 

As KSA continues to expand the industrial sector as part of 
Vision 2030 the project enables a hazardous industrial waste 
operator to capitalize on a growing segment on Saudi Arabia's 
economy

The opportunity allows a potential investor to deliver a 
greenfield project with no constraints from legacy 
infrastructure in a developing sector enabling a full use of 
best-in-class operational and technical solutions

Expected Investment size: 55M USD*

Plant capacity: 79,904 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 7.75 years

GDP Impact: 353M USD

Location (Region): Northern Borders Cluster

raw.title: NORTHERN BORDERS HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER
raw.description:
The opportunity aims to operate a healthcare waste treatment infrastructure across all Northern Borders cluster.

Driven by the Covid-19 health crisis, medical waste has 
increased to 2.6 M tons per day worldwide

Healthcare waste management market globally had a revenue 
of USD 12.8 bn in 2021. It is expected to be growing at a 
CAGR of 6.9% during the forecast period (2022-2030)

Market dynamics are also driven by the increasing use of 
reusable surgical products and rising awareness programs for 
medical waste management in developed countries

The project would require healthcare waste provided 
from public and private healthcare providers and 
transported to the facilities through waste collection 
and transfer operators in Northern Borders Cluster

Expansion and modernization of the healthcare 
sector are increasing the demand for healthcare 
waste management services

Growth in economic and population in KSA and 
further expansion of Northern Borders are 
additional demand drivers and are projected to 
increase in the future

Drive to increase public sector participation and 
competitiveness in the economy are further drivers 
for formulation of the opportunity
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 1M USD*

Plant capacity: 1,700 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 6.83 years

GDP Impact: 24M USD

Location (Region): Northern Borders Cluster

Northern Borders’s population is expected to continue to grow 
over the next few decades, which can potentially generate 
significant demand for the project

The investment opportunity focusses on creating waste 
treatment infrastructure, which provides a level of assurance 
while also offering attractive returns to potential investors

the overall waste generated across the globe

hazardous industrial waste from private waste collectors.

such as agricultural, healthcare and ELV waste.

for treatment of hazardous industrial waste

operators

expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Al Baha's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions

•
Local service providers’ expertise consists of mostly generalist, with

quality, wastewater, etc.

Upcoming spend of SAR ~3,4602 Bn and SAR ~5502 Bn in 
construction & manufacturing projects, respectively
•
NCEC has introduced EIA requirements for category 2 & 
3 projects as a prerequisite for obtaining project permits; 
this is expected to increase demand for EIA
•
Targeted growth of ~40% YoY in NCEC registered entities 
is expected to drive demand for env. services
•
Tadawul published environmental reporting guidelines 
for listed companies and PIF is increasingly reporting on 
sustainability across its entities
•

YoY across the period 2024 – 2030
•
Over 110 of EIA service providers are currently available, however, they 
remain insufficient to cover the market demand
•
Sustainability consulting market is dominated by local players; 
however, most of the market value is captured by experienced 
international companies offering specialized services
•
Global Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) market is growing 
rapidly, primarily driven by stricter regulatory compliance, and growing 
environmental awareness 
•
Integration of advanced digital technologies, such as AI and machine 
learning, in assessment processes
•
Utilization of remote sensing technologies, including satellite surveying, 
drones, and GIS
•
Incorporation of social dimensions by engaging indigenous and local 
communities in assessments

source_rows.title: JAZAN END OF LIFE TYRES TREATMENT FACILITY

raw.title: JAZAN END OF LIFE TYRES TREATMENT FACILITY
raw.description:
The aim of this opportunity is to create a waste tire treatment facility for the entire Jazan cluster.

Nearly one billion ELTs are generated worldwide annually, constituting 
more than 2% of the total amount of solid waste, and this waste flow is 
growing dynamically

The operation would require a stable input of end-of-life tires from 
producers for processing the waste

The rise in personal wealth and transforming consumer 
behavior in the Kingdom (increasing digitization, 
increasing personal consumption etc.) are increasing 
tire consumption requiring uplift in waste treatment 
solutions 

Waste management sector transformation driven by 
the Vision 2030 and initiatives to increase private 
sector participation require innovative, and sustainable 
solutions in KSA

The high level of economic and population growth in the KSA is 
expected to generate significant increase in consumption over the 
coming years, thus creating an opportunity for an end-of-life tire 
treatment facility operator to enter an attractive market

The Kingdom is placing a significant focus on the waste management 
sector as part of the Vision 2030 and the project can expect high level of 
engagement from the relevant authorities 
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 2M USD*

Plant capacity: 5,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 8.04 years

GDP Impact: 26M USD


source_rows.title: AL JOUF HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER

raw.title: AL JOUF HEALTHCARE WASTE TREATMENT CENTER
raw.description:
The opportunity aims to operate a healthcare waste treatment infrastructure across all Al Jouf cluster.

Driven by the Covid-19 health crisis, medical waste has 
increased to 2.6 M tons per day worldwide

Healthcare waste management market globally had a revenue 
of USD 12.8 bn in 2021. It is expected to be growing at a 
CAGR of 6.9% during the forecast period (2022-2030)

Market dynamics are also driven by the increasing use of 
reusable surgical products and rising awareness programs for 
medical waste management in developed countries

The project would require healthcare waste provided 
from public and private healthcare providers and 
transported to the facilities through waste collection 
and transfer operators in Al Jouf Cluster

Expansion and modernization of the healthcare 
sector are increasing the demand for healthcare 
waste management services

Growth in economic and population in KSA and 
further expansion of Al Jouf are additional 
demand drivers and are projected to increase in 
the future

Drive to increase public sector participation and 
competitiveness in the economy are further 
drivers for formulation of the opportunity
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 3M USD*

Plant capacity: 1,600 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 6.80 years

GDP Impact: 25M USD

Location (Region): Al Jouf Cluster

Al Jouf’s population is expected to continue to grow over the 
next few decades, which can potentially generate significant 
demand for the project

The investment opportunity focusses on creating waste 
treatment infrastructure, which provides a level of assurance 
while also offering attractive returns to potential investors

raw.title: WADI ALDAWASIR CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment and final disposal operator, offering services in Wadi Al 
Dawasir

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Wadi Al Dawasir's population growth and 
expansion are the main drivers of construction and 
demolition waste generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 4.62M USD*

Plant capacity: 150,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6.87 years

GDP Impact: 89M USD


source_rows.title: JEDDAH INERT LANDFILL

raw.title: JEDDAH INERT LANDFILL
raw.description:
The project aims to establish an inert landfill facility for construction and demolition waste in Jeddah.

The global construction and demolition waste management 
market size was $115 billion in 2020. The market is expected 
to reach $542.7 billion in 2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% of the 
total waste produced worldwide and is expected to grow at a 
rate of 3.2 billion tons per year until 2025

The main input to the operation comes from the 
Construction and Demolition Treatment facility for 
final disposal.


source_rows.title: PPP Opportunities Unveiled: Two Iconic Mixed-Use Developments in Al Madinah

raw.title: PPP Opportunities Unveiled: Two Iconic Mixed-Use Developments in Al Madinah
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 20/01/2025 Previous Next PPP Opportunities Unveiled: Two Iconic Mixed-Use Developments in Al Madinah Page Image launch of the Expressions of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for two transformative real estate projects in Al Madinah Al Munawarah: Joint Development Project in Sikkah Al Hadid, and Joint Development Project in Dhul Hulaifah. Page Content ​ Riyadh, January 2025: Al Madinah Regional Municipality, in collaboration with the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing (MOMAH) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of the Expressions of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for two transformative real estate projects in Al Madinah Al Munawarah: Joint Development Project in Sikkah Al Hadid, and Joint Development Project in Dhul Hulaifah. These projects will be executed under a Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) model through Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) contracts with a duration of 30 years. Sikkah Al Hadid project will transform an 84,657-square-meter government-owned site west of Al Madinah Al Munawarah into an integrated mixed-use facility. The site's strategic location and flexible zoning, permitting buildings up to 20 floors, combined with excellent road network connectivity, ensure easy access for residents and visitors. The development will also synergize with adjacent residential projects by the National Housing Company (NHC), supporting the surrounding community while catering to a growing population within a 5-kilometer radius. Key components include a state-of-the-art, four-story medical center with up to 200 beds, outpatient clinics, and multi-specialty services. Complementing these healthcare facilities is a shopping mall featuring diverse retail options, including fashion stores, food and beverage outlets, and entertainment venues. Dhul Hulaifah project is set to transform a 30,112-square-meter government-owned site into a mixed-use development just 6 kilometers from the Prophet's Mosque. This project leverages its picturesque surroundings, excellent connectivity, and proximity to religious landmarks, making it an ideal destination for residents and visitors. The development will feature a four-star hotel integrated with retail spaces and healthcare clinics, offering a unique blend of hospitality and essential services. Pedestrian-friendly retail areas will provide shopping, dining, and leisure options. Additionally, the project includes outpatient clinics offering specialized medical care, diagnostic services, a pharmacy, and a dedicated parking facility to ensure convenient access for all users. Local and international investors are invited to visit the NCP website at (investors.ncp.gov.sa​) for more information about these projects and to request the RFQ document. Interested investors should submit their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) by 2 March, 2025 at 11:59 pm KSA time. ​ ​ ​ Share | Print

Page Content ​ Riyadh, January 2025: Al Madinah Regional Municipality, in collaboration with the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing (MOMAH) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of the Expressions of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for two transformative real estate projects in Al Madinah Al Munawarah: Joint Development Project in Sikkah Al Hadid, and Joint Development Project in Dhul Hulaifah. These projects will be executed under a Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) model through Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) contracts with a duration of 30 years. Sikkah Al Hadid project will transform an 84,657-square-meter government-owned site west of Al Madinah Al Munawarah into an integrated mixed-use facility. The site's strategic location and flexible zoning, permitting buildings up to 20 floors, combined with excellent road network connectivity, ensure easy access for residents and visitors. The development will also synergize with adjacent residential projects by the National Housing Company (NHC), supporting the surrounding community while catering to a growing population within a 5-kilometer radius. Key components include a state-of-the-art, four-story medical center with up to 200 beds, outpatient clinics, and multi-specialty services. Complementing these healthcare facilities is a shopping mall featuring diverse retail options, including fashion stores, food and beverage outlets, and entertainment venues. Dhul Hulaifah project is set to transform a 30,112-square-meter government-owned site into a mixed-use development just 6 kilometers from the Prophet's Mosque. This project leverages its picturesque surroundings, excellent connectivity, and proximity to religious landmarks, making it an ideal destination for residents and visitors. The development will feature a four-star hotel integrated with retail spaces and healthcare clinics, offering a unique blend of hospitality and essential services. Pedestrian-friendly retail areas will provide shopping, dining, and leisure options. Additionally, the project includes outpatient clinics offering specialized medical care, diagnostic services, a pharmacy, and a dedicated parking facility to ensure convenient access for all users. Local and international investors are invited to visit the NCP website at (investors.ncp.gov.sa​) for more information about these projects and to request the RFQ document. Interested investors should submit their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) by 2 March, 2025 at 11:59 pm KSA time. ​ ​ ​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: MOMAH and NCP Launch EOI and RFQ for the Rehabilitation Operation and Maintenance of Public Parks PPP Project

raw.title: MOMAH and NCP Launch EOI and RFQ for the Rehabilitation Operation and Maintenance of Public Parks PPP Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 18/05/2026 Previous Next MOMAH and NCP Launch EOI and RFQ for the Rehabilitation Operation and Maintenance of Public Parks PPP Project Page Image Rehabilitating and operating public parks to enhance quality of life and urban sustainability in line with Vision 2030. Page Content ​ Riyadh, May 2026 – the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing (MOMAH) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), are pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for a new Public-Private Partnership (PPP) opportunity: Rehabilitation Operation and Maintenance of Public Parks PPP Project. The project covers 50 parks across three regions: Eastern Province, Jeddah, and Madinah. It will be implemented under a Rehabilitate, Operate, Maintain, and Transfer (ROMT) contract with a 15-year duration. The project encompasses the rehabilitation of park infrastructure, including green spaces, utilities, and recreational areas; the provision of operation and maintenance services, such as landscaping, cleaning, pest control, and quality assurance; the introduction of commercial facilities; as well as the procurement, supply, and maintenance of all necessary equipment required for operating the public parks. The project aims to elevate the quality and accessibility of municipal parks. It will also enhance the user experience and enable commercial activation that supports community engagement. Additionally, the project supports the Kingdom's broader Vision 2030 objectives by contributing to the delivery of high-quality municipal services, fostering urban sustainability, and promoting a balanced and vibrant living environment. MOMAH and NCP invite local and international investors to visit the NCP website at www.investors.​ncp.gov.sa for more information about the project and to request the RFQ document. Interested investors should submit their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) by July 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM, KSA time. Share | Print

source_rows.title: HAFAR AL BATIN END OF LIFE VEHICLES TREATMENT FACILITY

raw.title: HAFAR AL BATIN END OF LIFE VEHICLES TREATMENT FACILITY
raw.description:
The aim of this opportunity is to create a waste vehicles treatment facility for the entire Hafar Al Batin cluster.

Global automobile sales began to recover from their pandemic drop, 
reaching 66.7 M units sold in 2021. It is expected to decline in 2022, with 
a 2023 still below 2019

The operation would require a stable input of end-of-life vehicles from 
producers for processing and transfer along the further waste treatment 
value chain

The rise in personal wealth and transforming consumer 
behavior in the Kingdom (increasing digitization, increasing 
personal consumption etc.) are increasing vehicle 
consumption requiring uplift in waste treatment solutions 

Waste management sector transformation driven by the 
Vision 2030 and initiatives to increase private sector 
participation require innovative, and sustainable solutions 
in KSA

The high level of economic and population growth in the KSA is 
expected to generate significant increase in consumption over the 
coming years, thus creating an opportunity for an end-of-life vehicle 
treatment facility operator to enter an attractive market

The Kingdom is placing a significant focus on the waste management 
sector as part of the Vision 2030 and the project can expect high level of 
engagement from the relevant authorities 
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 13M USD*

Plant capacity: 20,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3%

Payback period: 8.51 years

GDP Impact: 101M USD

Location (Region): Hafar Al Batin Cluster

source_rows.title: Manufacturing of Specialty Medical Chairs and Parts

raw.title: Manufacturing of Specialty Medical Chairs and Parts

details.description: Establish local manufacturing of specialty medical chairs and components, including examination, surgical, dialysis, and rehabilitation chairs for hospitals, clinics, and long-term care centers. Targeted products include dentist chairs with built-in dental equipment, surgical and rehab seating.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Enhance availability of critical products by supporting the healthcare sector and ensuring stable local supply of specialty chairs and parts.
• Enable ecosystem activation by unlocking OEM and supplier growth through demand for localized parts (e.g., motors, control arms, hydraulic systems, medical-grade textiles).

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • Rising demand for customized chairs due to growth in clinics, surgical centers, and dialysis units. • Expansion of patient care infrastructure requiring procedure-specific seating systems.

source_rows.title: Local Manufacturing of Renal Care Devices

raw.title: Local Manufacturing of Renal Care Devices

details.description: Establish local manufacturing of hemodialysis machines and dialyzers—critical components for renal care systems supporting patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD). Targeted products include artificial kidney (dialysis) apparatus, dialyzers, peritoneal dialysis units, and CRRT systems.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Enhance availability of critical products and reduce long-term procurement costs.
• Strengthen national healthcare preparedness through local supply.
• Advance MedTech sector by positioning Saudi Arabia in precision mechatronics and patient monitoring technology.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • High and growing prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) across the population. • Increased hospital and clinic capacity driving demand for renal care devices. • Rising burden of non-communicable diseases requiring long-term dialysis treatments.

raw.title: Orthopedic Products Manufacturing

details.description: Establish local manufacturing of orthopedic products to support both surgical and non-surgical treatments of musculoskeletal conditions. Targeted products include head and spine orthopedic appliances, artificial joints, prosthetics, bionics, and orthotics.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Localize high-cost, high-precision devices to enhance accessibility and cost efficiency.
• Reduce dependency on imported orthopedic devices by manufacturing domestically.
• Position Saudi Arabia as a MedTech hub for sophisticated orthopedic solutions with regional export potential.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers

details.description: Establish local manufacturing for minimally invasive medical tools and devices such as disposable endoscopes, laparoscopic instruments, energy platforms, and associated consumables. The opportunity targets supplying healthcare providers with advanced surgical solutions that enhance precision, reduce recovery time, and improve patient outcomes.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Strengthen domestic healthcare self-sufficiency by reducing reliance on imported medical equipment.
• Enhance national emergency preparedness and supply chain resilience.
• Position KSA as a MedTech manufacturing hub with regional export potential and partnerships with OEMs.

source_rows.title: Residential and Retail Development Opportunities at Red Sea Project

raw.title: Residential and Retail Development Opportunities at Red Sea Project

details.description:
Deal Structure: Joint venture development partnership

Assets Under Consideration
- Luxury Residences: ~1,600 units.
- Luxury Retail and F&B Venues: 9,200 m².

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• The opportunity provides diverse retail and residential offerings which align with the spending habits of luxury travelers and residents. The opportunity targets the affluent consumer market for luxury residential and retail offerings in a prime tourist destination.
• The Red Sea Zone Authority is working to create Smart Destinations with state-of-the-art infrastructure, which enhance the attractiveness and accessibility for both residents and visitors.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - Increasing population and rising upper and middle-income segment point to a positive demand for luxury residential housing. - Surge in luxury tourism will drive further demand for residential, luxury retail and F&B experience, as visitors seek extended stays or consider secondary homes in the vicinity. - Strategic Location - the Red Sea is located north of Jeddah (~500 Km), and is within 8 hours flight time of 85% of the global population; further, newly created, dedicated airport will provide access and airlift to The Red Sea.

Saudi Jordanian Investment Company unveiled its pioneer project ‘The Kingdom Health’ in 2023, comprising of university with capacity of 600 students and hospital with 330 bed, 72 outpatient clinics and dedicated children’s hospital
