source_rows.title: RGA and NCP Launch EOI for Jeddah - Makkah Direct Highway Project

raw.title: RGA and NCP Launch EOI for Jeddah - Makkah Direct Highway Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 07/10/2024 Previous Next RGA and NCP Launch EOI for Jeddah - Makkah Direct Highway Project Page Image Riyadh, October 2024: Following the approval of the Supervisory Committee for Privatization in the Transport and Logistic Services Page Content Riyadh, October 2024: Following the approval of the Supervisory Committee for Privatization in the Transport and Logistic Services, chaired by H.E. Eng. Saleh bin Nasser Al-Jasser, Minister of Transport and Logistics Services and Chairman of the Roads General Authority (RGA), the RGA, in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for the Jeddah-Makkah Direct Highway project and its associated Motorway Services Areas (MSAs). The tender aims to attract the best in-class road construction companies, to be delivered to the highest standards of traffic safety and quality, in line with the Roads Strategy and the National Transport and Logistics Strategy (NTLS). RGA highlighted that the project will be executed through a public-private partnership (PPP) model, involving an Operations and Maintenance (O&M) contract for the Jeddah-Makkah Highway, along with a Design, Build, Finance, Operate, and Maintain (DBFOM) contract for new service areas on both sides of the highway, with a contract term of 10 years. It aims to operate and maintain the Jeddah-Makkah Direct Road, which consists of four lanes in each direction, spanning a distance of 64 kilometers, and includes six intersections, one camel crossing, and five vehicle overpasses. The project also includes the construction, operation, and maintenance of four service areas on both sides of the road. The Authority stated that the road will significantly serve pilgrims and Umrah performers heading to Makkah, as it is one of the shortest routes connecting Jeddah to the Holy City, taking just 35 minutes. The road will also contribute to supporting logistics and tourism in the region and will help maintain the Kingdom’s standing on the Global Connectivity Index. RGA and NCP invite local and international investors interested in road construction to learn about the project by visiting the NCP website and reviewing the EOI document on the project page. All interested companies should submit their EOI by October 24, 2024 at 3:00pm KSA time. -END- Share | Print

source_rows.title: Saudi Ministry of Education and National Center for Privatization launch first privatization project in the education sector

raw.title: Saudi Ministry of Education and National Center for Privatization launch first privatization project in the education sector
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 17/10/2024 Previous Next Saudi Ministry of Education and National Center for Privatization launch first privatization project in the education sector Page Image Saudi Ministry of Education, in cooperation with National Center for Privatization, launched the first privatization project in the education sector, Page Content Saudi Ministry of Education, in cooperation with National Center for Privatization, launched the first privatization project in the education sector, which is to assign the construction and operation of 60 new schools in Madinah to the private sector, with a total investment value of 5.2 billion riyals over 23 years, within a partnership contract between the public and private sectors. The project was launched under the patronage of Prince Saud bin Khalid bin Faisal, Deputy Emir of Madinah, and in the presence of Yousef Al-Bunyan, Minister of Education, and Muhannad bin Ahmed Basodan, CEO of the National Center for Privatization. The Minister, Yousef Al-Bunyan, confirmed that this project is one of the most important educational projects in the Kingdom, and comes within the framework of building, operating and converting schools in partnership with the private sector. The project is the first of its kind in the education sector in the Kingdom and targets 60 school buildings fully equipped with advanced educational services and facilities, which inaugurates a new phase in the privatization of services, improving performance and raising operational efficiency, while providing the finest services to male and female students and their families. Al-Bunyan added that the ministry is currently working on transferring operational services to the Buildings Development Company, the executive arm of the ministry, with the aim of focusing on improving the educational process and ensuring high-quality educational outcomes.​ He also thanked the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and his loyal Crown Prince, for the great support and continuous follow-up that education enjoys. For his part, Muhannad bin Ahmed Basudan, CEO of the National Center for Privatization, stressed that the patronage of the Emir of Madinah for the inauguration ceremony of 60 modern schools, with advanced equipment and in accordance with international standards, reflects the state’s commitment to enhancing national investments and supporting the economy by providing attractive investment opportunities for the private sector. He pointed out that this project contributes to increasing the private sector’s contribution to the GDP and enhances the sustainability of the Kingdom’s economy. Basudan explained that the first phase of the project has been successfully operated, as 30 schools received male and female students in the current academic year 1446/1447 AH, while 30 other schools are preparing to receive students in the second phase next year. He added that these efforts contribute to the development of a modern educational infrastructure, designed to meet the needs of new generations and provide high-quality education in a model educational environment. The project include: 32 primary schools, 17 intermediate schools, 6 secondary schools, and 5 kindergartens, all accommodating 52,000 male and female students. These schools have been equipped according to the highest quality and safety standards, to ensure the health and safety of students, teachers, employees and visitors, ensuring a safe and sustainable educational environment. It is worth noting that the strategic partnership between the Ministry of Education and the Buildings Development Company, with the support of the National Center for Privatization, aims to achieve the “Taiba without Rented Buildings” initiative, which aims to reach zero percent of rented schools by 2025, within the framework of the goals of the Kingdom’s Vision 2030. The project seeks to replace rented buildings with advanced government educational projects that contribute to achieving quality education and the highest levels of learning. Share | Print

raw.title: MATARAT Holding, in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) announce the launch of Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for the New Taif International Airport
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 02/12/2024 Previous Next MATARAT Holding, in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) announce the launch of Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for the New Taif International Airport Page Image Expression of Interest (EOI) for the new Taif International Airport project. Page Content ​ Riyadh, December 2024: MATARAT Holding, in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) is pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) for the new Taif International Airport project. This invitation is open to interested private sector entities in a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model under a Build-Transfer-Operate (BTO) contract for a period of 30 years inclusive of the construction period. This Project is in line with Vision 2030's goals, which aims to enhance the growth of the aviation sector in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Through the National Transport and Logistics Strategy and the National Aviation Strategy, the Kingdom seeks to strengthen its position among the leading nations as a global logistics hub connecting three continents. The new Taif International Airport will be located 21 km southeast of the existing Taif Airport, with a capacity to accommodate 2.5 million passengers by 2030. The Project scope includes (BTO) model of the new airport. The proposed design features a runway with a full-length-parallel taxiway, that connects to a single commercial apron. The new Taif International Airport will include a well-equipped commercial passenger terminal building aligned with the airport's projected capacity and demand, along with facility buildings, utility networks, car parks, and access roads that enable the standard operation of the airport. The project includes additional expansions to meet future subsystem requirements. The new Taif International Airport is expected to meet the projected increase in demand by 2055. It is also expected to meet the needs of Umrah pilgrims as a viable alternative within the region's multi-airport system. This system includes King Abdulaziz Airport in Jeddah, Prince Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Airport in Madinah, and Prince Abdulmohsen bin Abdulaziz Airport in Yanbu. The new Taif International Airport will contribute to the economic development of Taif city and its surrounding areas, in line with the National Aviation Strategy, as a highly efficient airport offering a top-quality passenger experience MATARAT Holding and NCP invite interested investors to review the EOI document containing project information by visiting the NCP's website (www.ncp.gov.sa). The deadline for submission of EOIs is January 10 2025, at 3:00 p.m. KSA time.​​ ​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: NCP Partners with Universities and Celebrates CP3P Certification Holders

raw.title: NCP Partners with Universities and Celebrates CP3P Certification Holders
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 25/12/2024 Previous Next NCP Partners with Universities and Celebrates CP3P Certification Holders Page Image The signing ceremony also celebrated the achievement of the recipients of the (CP3P) certification. This internationally recognized certification equips professionals with the knowledge and skills necessary to successfully navigate the PPP landscape. Page Content ​ The National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), represented by CEO Mohannad Basodan and Vice President for Strategic Marketing and Knowledge Management Hani Alsaigh, signed cooperation agreements with Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University (PNU) and Al Yamamah University. The agreements were signed by Vice Rector for Academic Affairs Dr. Farah Al-Askar representing PNU, and Abdulrahman Al-Khudair, CEO of Al Yamamah University. These partnerships aim to integrate privatization and public-private partnership (PPP) concepts into university curricula, offer student internships, and conduct joint research. The signing ceremony also celebrated the achievement of the recipients of the (CP3P) certification. This internationally recognized certification equips professionals with the knowledge and skills necessary to successfully navigate the PPP landscape, including project development, evaluation, and contract management, enabling them to execute their responsibilities in line with best practices. Mr. Basodan emphasized the NCP's commitment to developing a skilled workforce in the PPP sector. "By collaborating with universities and acknowledging the achievements of CP3P-certified professionals, we contribute to fostering a thriving PPP ecosystem. This raises awareness of the importance of PPP projects and creates an investment environment that attracts both local and international investors by effectively leveraging PPP opportunities within the Kingdom," he stated. He also noted that the NCP has conducted 11 specialized CP3P training workshops, benefiting over 100 professionals from various sectors. Dr. Al-Askar, stated that the partnership with the NCP represents a step forward in keeping pace with the evolving labor market. This is achieved by enriching educational curricula with concepts related to the PPP field, bridging the gap between learning outcomes and market demands, increasing cooperative training opportunities for students at the center, and supporting specialized research to ​create added value for society. Mr. Al-khudair mentioned that this partnership enables universities to deliver exceptional outputs in terms of research, studies, and specialized human resources. This aligns with the role of the private sector in preparing highly skilled national talents capable of competing within the context of the Kingdom's economic growth and expansion. This is achieved in an attractive educational and research environment and through partnerships adhering to the highest standards. The NCP seeks to foster stronger academic-industry partnerships with Saudi universities, demonstrating its commitment to developing human capital. These efforts align with the dynamic needs of the workforce and contribute to building the national economy, advancing the knowledge-based economy, and achieving the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030. ​ ​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: MODON and NCP Launch EOI for Logistics Zone Development in Dammam 2nd Industrial City

raw.title: MODON and NCP Launch EOI for Logistics Zone Development in Dammam 2nd Industrial City
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 09/03/2025 Previous Next MODON and NCP Launch EOI for Logistics Zone Development in Dammam 2nd Industrial City Page Image Launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) for the Logistics Zone Development in Dammam 2nd Industrial City. Page Content ​​ Riyadh, February 2025 – Saudi Authority for Industrial Cities and Technology Zones “MODON", in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) for the Logistics Zone Development in Dammam 2 nd Industrial City. This project will be executed under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model through a Design-Build-Finance-Operate–Maintain-Transfer (DBFOMT) contract with a period of 30 years. The Logistics Zone Development Project aims to enhance the Kingdom's logistics infrastructure to support Saudi Arabia's vision of becoming a global logistics hub. Spanning approximately 850,000 square meters, the project is strategically located within Dammam 2 nd Industrial City and will serve as a key enabler for trade, cross-border connectivity, and industrial expansion. The development will include modern logistics facilities, warehousing solutions, and operate and maintain the infrastructure, ensuring seamless integration with both existing and future industrial activities. The site will comprise, among other components, a gated public area, a non-gated public area, leasable spaces, and a dedicated utilities infrastructure area. As part of the project scope, the private sector partner will be responsible for securing financing, designing and constructing leasable areas, and maintaining infrastructure, managing operations and maintenance, and commercializing the project through tenant attraction, leasing, and revenue generation. This project aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 by fostering private sector participation, driving economic diversification, and strengthening the country's logistics ecosystem. Local and international investors are invited to visit the NCP website at ( www.ncp.gov.sa ) for more information about the project. The deadline for submitting EOIs is March 9 2025, at 3:00 p.m. KSA time. ​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: NCP Showcases Saudi Arabia

raw.title: NCP Showcases Saudi Arabia
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 07/04/2025 Previous Next NCP Showcases Saudi Arabia's PPP Investment Landscape and Opportunities in the US Page Image Participated in the 2025 Public-Private Partnership Conference & Expo (P3C) held in Dallas, Texas Page Content ​ Riyadh, April, 2025 – The National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) participated in the 2025 Public-Private Partnership Conference & Expo (P3C) held in Dallas, Texas from April 7-9. This participation is part of NCP's ongoing efforts to expand private sector involvement in infrastructure and public service projects, in line with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 objectives. P3C is the premier and largest annual conference focused on public-private partnerships (PPP). It brings together leading public and private sector developers, decision-makers, as well as professionals from the construction, engineering, consultancy, and legal sectors operating in PPPs. With over 1,000 attendees and nearly 400 companies, P3C serves as a global hub for knowledge exchange and investment exploration. The event provided a valuable platform for NCP's inaugural participation in two key sessions in the conference. The first session, co-presented by representatives from NCP and the Ministry of Investment, offered a comprehensive overview of the Kingdom's evolving economic landscape and its expanding PPP program. It also highlighted projects from amongst 200 investment opportunities across various sectors, including water, transportation, logistics, real estate, and sports, with a total estimated investment value of USD 190 billion. The second session focused on the PPP landscape in Saudi Arabia compared to the US, addressing recent regulatory advancements, current sector trends, and future prospects. NCP experts shared their valuable insights and engaged with stakeholders on potential collaboration avenues. The NCP delegation also held meetings with several US companies, and organizations such as Fluor, Fengate, and John Laing, amongst others. These meetings, also attended by representatives from Riyad Bank's Houston branch, aimed to explore potential areas of interest for participating companies while showcasing NCP's extensive project portfolio and the strong support from the Kingdom's banking sector. As Saudi Arabia's leading entity for privatization and PPP, NCP continues to play a pivotal role in unlocking new opportunities for international investors and developers to contribute to Saudi Arabia's ambitious development journey in advancing infrastructure and improving public service delivery. ​ Share | Print

raw.title: MoD and NCP Launch EOI and RFQ for Riyadh Administrative Office Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 11/05/2025 Previous Next MoD and NCP Launch EOI and RFQ for Riyadh Administrative Office Project Page Image announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for the Riyadh Administrative Office Project for MoD personnel Page Content ​ Riyadh, May 2025: The Ministry of Defense (MoD), in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for the Riyadh Administrative Office Project for MoD personnel. The project will be developed through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model under a Design, Build, Finance, and Maintain (DBFM) contract. The contract term will extend for 27.5 years, after which the project will be transferred to the Ministry. Located in North Riyadh, the project covers approximately 52,793 square meters and will accommodate about 4,500 employees, with 3,200 dedicated parking spaces. The private sector partner will be responsible for the design, construction, and maintenance of the office buildings and supporting infrastructure, as well as coordinating with stakeholders and obtaining the required permits from the government. The project aims to establish a high-quality, sustainable work environment that aligns with modern design standards. MoD and NCP invite local and international investors to visit the NCP website at (www.ncp.gov.sa) for more information about the project and to request the RFQ document. Interested investors should submit their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) by 3 June, 2025, at 3:00 p.m. KSA time. ​ ​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: NCP and AIAI Partner to Advance PPP Expertise and US Private Sector Engagement

raw.title: NCP and AIAI Partner to Advance PPP Expertise and US Private Sector Engagement
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 15/05/2025 Previous Next NCP and AIAI Partner to Advance PPP Expertise and US Private Sector Engagement Page Image NCP has formalized a partnership with the Association for the Improvement of American Infrastructure (AIAI) Page Content Riyadh, May 2025 – The National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) has formalized a partnership with the Association for the Improvement of American Infrastructure (AIAI) by signing a memorandum of cooperation (MoC) to strengthen professional development in privatization and public-private partnerships (PPPs) and deepen engagement with the US private sector. The agreement was signed during NCP's participation in the Saudi-US Investment Forum, held in Riyadh on May 13, 2025, as part of President Trump's visit to the Kingdom. Hosted at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center, the Forum brought together leading Saudi and American investors to celebrate a bilateral relationship nearly a century in the making. Program highlights included ministerial sessions, CEO panels, and discussions covering clean energy, artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, digital infrastructure, biotechnology, defense, finance, and health. The MoC was signed by Mr. Mohannad Basodan, CEO of NCP, and Ms. Lisa Buglione, Executive Director of AIAI. It reflects NCP's continued commitment to aligning with international best practices and fostering cross-border knowledge exchange. AIAI is a nonprofit organization composed of leading infrastructure experts in the US, dedicated to advancing the use of the PPP model through a hands-on, action-driven approach. The organization provides education, resources, and advisory tools to equip public and private stakeholders with the knowledge needed to successfully deliver infrastructure projects. Under the agreement, NCP and AIAI will collaborate to develop and issue professional certification programs, establish a specialized “Train-the-Trainers" program to build national PPP expertise, and broaden access to the US private sector through AIAI's extensive network of members and institutional resources. The MoC will also support mutual knowledge sharing through joint participation in events, expert visits, organization of forums, and specialized sessions, as well as other mutually agreed initiatives. Commenting on the partnership, Mr. Basodan stated: “This collaboration represents a key step forward in NCP's mission to institutionalize global best practices in PPP and expand international engagement. By collaborating with AIAI, we are reinforcing our commitment to building a world-class PPP ecosystem—one that enables knowledge transfer, empowers Saudi professionals, and unlocks new opportunities for US private sector participation in the Kingdom's upcoming infrastructure agenda, in line with Saudi Vision 2030". Commenting on this, Ms. Lisa Buglione mentioned that: “AIAI has spent years building a coalition of experienced voices committed to strengthening infrastructure through PPPs. We're honored to support NCP as they lead efforts to expand PPPs and continue to drive infrastructure investment in the Kingdom. I want to recognize Thomas Sherman, Director of AIAI's Education and Advisory services who lead the effort to cultivate this unique partnership. We look forward to sharing global best practices and supporting the NCP as they advance Saudi Vision 2030".​ ​ Share | Print

raw.title: MOMAH in Collaboration with Ashraq Development Company and NCP Launches EOI Phase for King Fahd Suburb Boulevard in Dammam Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 29/06/2025 Previous Next MOMAH in Collaboration with Ashraq Development Company and NCP Launches EOI Phase for King Fahd Suburb Boulevard in Dammam Project Page Image Spanning approximately 1,000,000 m², the project will be developed in two phases, with a balanced allocation of a development plots, green spaces, and infrastructure facilities. Page Content ​​​​​ Riyadh, June 2025 – The Ministry of Municipalities and Housing (MOMAH), in collaboration with Ashraq Development Company — the development arm of the Eastern Province Municipality — and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for the King Fahd Suburb Boulevard in Dammam Project. This Public-Private Partnership (PPP) project will be delivered under a Design, Build, Finance, Operate, Maintain, and Transfer (DBFOMT) model, with a contract term of 30 years. Spanning approximately 1,000,000 m², the project will be developed in two phases, with a balanced allocation of a development plots, green spaces, and infrastructure facilities. The project also features a 4 km integrated mixed-use zone along a central boulevard and linear parklands, forming part of a larger 7.3 km corridor. Leveraging its strategic location and potential to deliver a unique urban experience, the private sector partner will be responsible for developing and operating a comprehensive mixed-use environment. This will include leisure and recreational facilities, public parks, entertainment venues, retail outlets, office spaces, hospitality zones, pedestrian walkways, and road networks—all designed to foster a vibrant and inclusive community in the Eastern Province. The project is poised to redefine the urban landscape of the King Fahd Suburb in Dammam, advancing Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 goals to enhance quality of life, drive sustainable development, and increase private sector participation in municipal infrastructure. Interested local and international investors are invited to review the EOI document, available on the NCP website at: www.investors.ncp.gov.sa . The deadline for submitting EOIs is 16 July, 2025 at 11:59 p.m. KSA time. ​​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: HMM in Collaboration with MOMAH and NCP Launches EOI and RFQ for Mixed-Use Development in Makkah

raw.title: HMM in Collaboration with MOMAH and NCP Launches EOI and RFQ for Mixed-Use Development in Makkah
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 29/06/2025 Previous Next HMM in Collaboration with MOMAH and NCP Launches EOI and RFQ for Mixed-Use Development in Makkah Page Image Strategically located along Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Road (Makkah – Alhada) near the Al Awali District, the government-owned site spans approximately 220,000 square meters . Page Content Riyadh, June 2025: The Holy Makkah Municipality (HMM), in collaboration with the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing (MOMAH) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) and Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for the Joint Development Project on Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Road (Makkah – Alhada), a major mixed-use development opportunity in Makkah. The project will be implemented through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model under a Build-Own- Operate- Transfer (BOOT) contract with a 30-year term. The private sector partner will be responsible for the design, financing, construction, operation, and maintenance of the development. Upon completion of the contract term, the fully operational project will be transferred to HMM. Strategically located along Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz Road (Makkah – Alhada) near the Al Awali District, the government-owned site spans approximately 220,000 square meters and offers direct access to the Holy Mosque while avoiding the congestion of Makkah's city center. Its proximity to major commercial hubs, landmarks, and planned developments makes it a prime location for large-scale investment. The development will include a regional shopping mall with diverse retail, dining, and entertainment options, alongside big-box outlets for home improvement, electronics, furniture, and lifestyle products. It will also include two hospitals, a 200-bed long-term care facility and a 100-bed multi-specialty hospital, complemented by road infrastructure, landscaped open spaces, and parking for approximately 2,800 cars. Leveraging the expertise of the private sector, this project is expected to enhance Makkah's infrastructure and improve access to healthcare and commercial services. It will also contribute to the Kingdom's broader goals by improving services provided for residents and visitors, while expanding non-oil revenue streams in line with Saudi Vision 2030. Local and international investors are invited to visit the NCP website at www.​investors.ncp.gov.sa for more information about the project and to request the RFQ document. Interested investors should submit their Statement of Qualification (SOQ) by 27 July, 2025 at 3:00 PM, KSA time. Share | Print

source_rows.title: RGA and NCP Launch EOI for One-Stop Station PPP Project

raw.title: RGA and NCP Launch EOI for One-Stop Station PPP Project
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 08/07/2025 Previous Next RGA and NCP Launch EOI for One-Stop Station PPP Project Page Image The project will be executed under a 30-year Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain (DBFOM) contract and tendered in three separate waves, comprising six packages. Page Content Riyadh, July 2025: Following the approval of the Transport and Logistic Services Privatization Supervisory Committee, chaired by H.E. Eng. Saleh bin Nasser Al-Jasser, Minister of Transport and Logistics Services, the Roads General Authority (RGA), in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) phase for the One-Stop Station (OSS) Public-Private Partnership (PPP) project. The project will be executed under a 30-year Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain (DBFOM) contract and tendered in three separate waves, comprising six packages. The packages are of similar scope and transaction structure, with a phased procurement approach designed to ensure a competitive bidding process that fosters private sector innovation. The first wave will include the initial package; the second wave will encompass the second and third packages; and the third wave will cover the remaining three packages. The project involves the development of roadside service facilities across various locations within RGA's 73,600-kilometer intercity road network. These facilities will include refueling stations, commercial spaces, parking lots, driver rest areas, vehicle maintenance services, and hospitality amenities. This promising opportunity is open to both local and international investors interested in contributing to the Kingdom's infrastructure modernization. The launch of the first wave will be detailed in the upcoming Request for Qualification (RFQ) stage. Through this initiative, Saudi Arabia aims to establish a modern, efficient, and traveler-friendly road network while reinforcing private sector participation in line with the National Transport and Logistics Strategy, as well as Vision 2030.​ RGA and NCP invite interested local and international investors to review the EOI document, available on the NCP website at www.investors.ncp.gov.sa . The deadline for submitting EOIs is 28 July, 2025, at 11:59 p.m. KSA time. ​ Share | Print

These steps reflect the Ministry of Sport's commitment to achieving the goals of the Sports Clubs Investment and Privatization Project. raw.title: MATARAT Holding & NCP Launch EoI for The Development of Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Qassim
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 09/02/2026 Previous Next MATARAT Holding & NCP Launch EoI for The Development of Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Qassim Page Image Aims to enhance the growth of the aviation sector in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Page Content ​​ Under the supervision of the Supervisory Committee for Privatization in the Transport and Logistics Services Sector chaired by His Excellency the Minister of Transport and Logistics Services, Eng. Saleh Nasser Al-Jasser, MATARAT Holding, in collaboration with the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of Expression of Interest (EOI) stage for the development of Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport Public Private Partnership Project, inviting bids from local, regional, and international private sector participants for a contract duration of 30 years, including the construction phase. His Excellency, the President of the General Authority of Civil Aviation and Chairman of the Board of MATARAT Holding, Mr. Abdulaziz bin Abdullah Al-Duailej, stated that the issuance of the Request for Expression of Interest reflects the civil aviation system's commitment to empowering and engaging the private sector, while fostering high value investment partnerships in the airport sector. He emphasized that this step would help enhance infrastructure development, improve operational efficiency, and elevate the quality of services provided to travelers. His Excellency further highlighted that the development project of Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Qassim represents a strategic initiative that supports the objectives of the Aviation Program stems from the National Transport and Logistics Strategy. The project, he noted, underscores the aviation ecosystem's dedication to attracting both local and international investments, strengthening the competitiveness of regional airports, and advancing economic and tourism growth across the Kingdom, in alignment with the goals of Saudi Vision 2030. Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport development project aligns with Vision 2030's goals which aims to enhance the growth of the aviation sector in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Through the National Transport and Logistics Strategy and the Aviation Program derived from it, the Kingdom seeks to strengthen its position among the leading nations as a global logistics hub connecting three continents. The project scope includes the development and operation of Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport, covering design, financing, construction, transfer, operations and maintenance. The project site is located 25 kilometers from Buraidah in the Qassim region, and the proposed scope includes a fully equipped passenger terminal to accommodate the airport's expected demand, along with supporting service facilities and the development of airside infrastructure, including runway, taxiways, and aprons. Once ready, the redeveloped airport will create additional capacity to handle a projected increase in annual traffic, playing a key role in enabling the Kingdom's rapid economic transformation and boosting its rising stature as a major destination for business and tourism.​ Local and international investors are invited to visit the NCP website at ( investors.ncp.gov.sa ) for more information about the project and to request the EOI document. Interested investors should submit their EOI by 23/02/2026 at 11:59 PM KSA time.​ ​ Share | Print

raw.title: MOMAH and NCP Launch EOI to Municipal Food Safety Labs Across Five Municipalities in Saudi Arabia
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 01/04/2026 Previous Next MOMAH and NCP Launch EOI to Municipal Food Safety Labs Across Five Municipalities in Saudi Arabia Page Image Developing advanced food safety labs to enhance testing, ensure quality, and protect public health in line with Vision 2030. Page Content Riyadh, April 2026 , the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing (MOMAH) and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), have announced the launch of the Expression of Interest (EOI) stage for the Municipal Food Safety Labs Operation Project under a PPP framework (Equip-Operate-Maintain-Transfer) for a contract duration of 5 years, inviting local, regional, and global companies with experience in lab operations to participate and submit their bids. The project scope includes equipping, operating, and maintaining food safety labs across five municipalities, including Hafr Al Batin, Northern Borders, Tabuk, Qassim, and Al Ahsa. The project aims to upgrade lab equipment, expand chemical and microbiological testing capacity for food and water products, ensure testing accuracy to support the lab compliance value chain, and facilitate ongoing knowledge transfer and end-of-contract handover to the respective municipalities. The Municipal Food Safety Labs Operation Project seeks to boost public health and safety standards for the Kingdom's citizens and residents in line with the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030, besides developing the municipal monitoring ecosystem, optimizing food and water testing, and empowering the private sector to run operations as per global best practices. Once completed, the project will enhance food safety in the Kingdom, enable sustainable growth across targeted regions by creating unique investment opportunities for the private sector, and improve the efficiency of government spending through the PPP model, playing a key role in elevating the quality of municipal services being offered to citizens and residents. source_rows.title: MWAN and NCP Launch EOI for Development and Operation of the National Digital Waste Management Platform

raw.title: MWAN and NCP Launch EOI for Development and Operation of the National Digital Waste Management Platform
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 15/04/2026 Previous Next MWAN and NCP Launch EOI for Development and Operation of the National Digital Waste Management Platform Page Image A PPP project to develop a unified digital platform enhancing waste management efficiency across the Kingdom. Page Content Riyadh: April 2026 - The National Center for Waste Management (MWAN), in collaboration with the Ministry of Environment, Water & Agriculture (MEWA), the Environment Fund, and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), is pleased to announce the launch of Expression of Interest (EOI) stage to develop and operate the National Digital Waste Management Platform under a PPP framework (Design, Build, Finance, Operate, Maintain, and Transfer) for a contract duration of 11 years, inviting local and global companies and investors to review the opportunity and submit their responses. This project represents a strategic milestone aimed at strengthening the planning, regulation, monitoring, and optimization of waste management activities across the Kingdom. Under the project, the private sector partner will be responsible for designing, developing, financing, operating, and maintaining a nationwide integrated digital platform, enabling effective coordination, governance, and integration across the entire waste management value chain. The project scope includes the deployment of a comprehensive suite of digital services, comprising seven (7) core business applications with twenty-seven (27) functional modules. The platform will support user and stakeholder management, customer classification, licensing systems, electronic waste tracking (e-manifest), regulatory reporting and data analytics, marketplace functionalities, and smart contracts. The platform will serve as a centralized system covering data collection, reporting, analytics, compliance monitoring, and stakeholder integration across the waste management value chain. The project aims to expand digital coverage of waste management activities, enhance operational efficiency and service quality, and streamline regulatory and compliance processes. This initiative reinforces Saudi Arabia's commitment to sustainable and efficient waste management practices and supports the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030 by advancing sustainability and accelerating digital transformation within the sector. Local and international investors, financial institutions, and operators are invited to visit the MWAN website at https://mwan.gov.sa/ for more information about the project and to request the EOI document. Interested investors should submit their EOI by 6 May 2026, at 11:59 PM KSA time. ​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: Ministry of Sport and National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) Announce Offering of Five Additional Clubs for Privatization

raw.title: Ministry of Sport and National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) Announce Offering of Five Additional Clubs for Privatization
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 08/06/2026 Previous Next Ministry of Sport and National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) Announce Offering of Five Additional Clubs for Privatization Page Image offering of five sports clubs to investors: Al-Riyadh, Abha, Al-Fateh, Al-Tai, and Al-Shoulla. The offering includes the receipt of expressions of interest and prequalification submissions from entities seeking to acquire these clubs Page Content ​​ The Ministry of Sport and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) announced today, Monday 8 June 2026, the offering of five sports clubs to investors: Al-Riyadh, Abha, Al-Fateh, Al-Tai, and Al-Shoulla. The offering includes the receipt of expressions of interest and prequalification submissions from entities seeking to acquire these clubs, as part of the ongoing Sports Clubs Investment and Privatization Project and efforts to open the door for the private sector to capitalize on promising opportunities within the sports sector. The Ministry revealed that the five clubs have completed all required regulatory procedures and have reached the readiness stage for offering to investors. It also noted that the deadline for receiving prequalification applications from interested investment entities is Sunday, 5 July 2026. Interested investors can submit prequalification applications through the NCP's website via the following link: investors​.ncp.gov.sa . The Ministry emphasized that sports clubs are being prepared to enter the project through a comprehensive framework that takes into account the readiness level of each club individually, as well as the seriousness and preparedness of potential investors. This approach ensures the fulfillment of all requirements necessary to participate in the project, while enhancing the efficiency of the offering process and generating sustainable value for both sports clubs and investors. The Ministry also confirmed that expressions of interest for the acquisition of any sports club remain open on an ongoing basis in accordance with the project's procedures and regulations. It noted that, where interest has been expressed in a particular club, the offering process typically takes between 8 and 10 months. The Ministry further highlighted the strong interest shown by both local and international investors in acquiring sports clubs, with more than 80 expressions of interest registered to date across 22 sports clubs. This reflects the project's rapid growth and the opportunities available for private sector entities to contribute to the continued development of the sports sector. Regarding the latest developments concerning Al-Najma and Al-Akhdoud clubs, the Ministry explained that negotiations are currently underway and will be followed by the contract-signing phase, ahead of the official announcement of the transfer of ownership of the two clubs to their new owners.​ Share | Print

raw.title: MATARAT Holding and National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) announce the launch of Request for Proposals (RFP) phase to the qualified bidders for the New Taif International Airport
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 09/06/2026 Previous Next MATARAT Holding and National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) announce the launch of Request for Proposals (RFP) phase to the qualified bidders for the New Taif International Airport Page Image The new Taif International Airport will contribute to the economic development of Taif city and its surrounding areas, in line with the National Aviation Strategy, as a highly efficient airport offering top-quality passenger experience. Page Content Riyadh, June 2026: MATARAT Holding and the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP) are pleased to announce the launch of the Request for Proposals (RFP) for the new Taif International Airport project. This invitation is open to interested private sector entities in a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model under a Build-Transfer-Operate (BTO) contract for a period of 30 years inclusive of the construction period. This Project is in line with Vision 2030's goals, which aims to enhance the growth of the aviation sector in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Through the National Transport and Logistics Strategy and the National Aviation Strategy, the Kingdom seeks to strengthen its position among the leading nations as a global logistics hub connecting three continents. The new Taif International Airport will be located 21 km southeast of the existing Taif Airport, with a capacity to accommodate 2.5 million passengers by 2030. The Project scope includes (BTO) model of the new airport. The proposed design features a runway with a full-length-parallel taxiway, that connects to a single commercial apron. The new Taif International Airport will include a well-equipped commercial passenger terminal building aligned with the airport's projected capacity and demand, along with facility buildings, utility networks, car parks, and access roads that enable the standard operation of the airport. The project includes additional expansions to meet future subsystem requirements. The new Taif International Airport is expected to meet the projected increase in demand by 2055. It is also expected to meet the needs of Umrah pilgrims as a viable alternative within the region's multi-airport system. This system includes King Abdulaziz Airport in Jeddah, Prince Mohammed bin Abdulaziz Airport in Madinah, and Prince Abdulmohsen bin Abdulaziz Airport in Yanbu. The new Taif International Airport will contribute to the economic development of Taif city and its surrounding areas, in line with the National Aviation Strategy, as a highly efficient airport offering top-quality passenger experience. ​ ​ Share | Print

Situated in a prime location southeast of Makkah, the site is zoned for two-story developments and features excellent connectivity to major road networks, ensuring seamless accessibility from all parts of the city. Furthermore, the development will integrate services with surrounding projects to address community needs, deliver essential services, and support ongoing population growth. Local and international investors, financial institutions, and operators are invited to visit the NCP website at investors​​.ncp.gov.sa for more information about the project and to request the EOI document. source_rows.title: RFQ Launched for King Fahd Suburb Boulevard PPP Project in Eastern Province

raw.title: RFQ Launched for King Fahd Suburb Boulevard PPP Project in Eastern Province
raw.raw_text: News Return to Media Center 27/08/2026 Previous Next RFQ Launched for King Fahd Suburb Boulevard PPP Project in Eastern Province Page Image Spanning approximately 1,000,000 m², the project will be developed in two phases, with a balanced allocation of a development plots, green spaces, and infrastructure facilities. Page Content Riyadh, August 2026 ​ – The Ministry of Municipalities and Housing (MOMAH), the National Center for Privatization & PPP (NCP), and Ashraq Development Company, the development arm of the Eastern Province Municipality, are pleased to announce the launch of the Request for Qualification (RFQ) phase for the King Fahd Suburb Boulevard Project in the Eastern Province. This Public-Private Partnership (PPP) project will be delivered under a Design, Build, Finance, Operate, Maintain, and Transfer (DBFOMT) model, with a contract term of 43 years. Located in Al Bayda Governorate in the Eastern Province, the project spans approximately 1,000,000 m² and will be developed in two phases, with a balanced allocation of development plots, green spaces, and infrastructure facilities. The project also features a 4 km integrated mixed-use zone along a central boulevard and linear parklands, forming part of a larger 7.3 km corridor. Leveraging its strategic location and potential to deliver a unique urban experience, the private sector partner will be responsible for developing and operating a comprehensive mixed-use environment. This will include leisure and recreational facilities, public parks, entertainment venues, retail outlets, office spaces, and road networks—all designed to foster a vibrant environment in the Eastern Province. ​​The project is poised to redefine the urban landscape of the King Fahd Suburb in Dammam, advancing Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 goals to enhance quality of life, drive sustainable development, and increase private sector participation in municipal infrastructure. For more information about the project, interested parties can visit the Investors Portal on the NCP website at: www.Investors.ncp.gov.sa For inquiries or submissions, you may reach out via email at kingfahadblvd@ashraq.sa The deadline for submitting the Statement of Qualification (SOQ) is 22 October 2026 at 11:59​ Share | Print

source_rows.title: توسعة وتطوير مطار العلا الدولي: فرصة استثمارية للشراكة بين القطاع العام والخاص

raw.titleEN: AlUla international Airport Expansion – PPP Investment Opportunity
raw.titleAR: توسعة وتطوير مطار العلا الدولي: فرصة استثمارية للشراكة بين القطاع العام والخاص
raw.descriptionEN:
In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the expansion of AlUla International Airport to support economic and tourism growth and enhance AlUla’s air connectivity.
The project includes a new passenger terminal of approximately 30,000 sqm, with a capacity of up to 3 million passengers annually, a 5,000 sqm cargo terminal incorporating world-class equestrian facilities, a private aviation terminal of approximately 10,000 sqm, general aviation and helicopter facilities, and an extension of the runway to 3,000 metres, in addition to roads, parking, maintenance facilities, utilities, and fuel facilities.
Approximately 1 million sqm of land is also available for complementary commercial uses, including logistics, retail, hospitality, and aviation services.
The project is planned to be delivered under a Build–Transfer–Operate (BTO) model, with a concession period of up to 35 years
The RFP is expected to be launched in Q3 2027, with project completion targeted by 2032
raw.descriptionAR:
تماشيًا مع خطة التخصيص المعتمدة من المركز الوطني للتخصيص، تعمل الهيئة الملكية لمحافظة العلا على توسعة مطار العلا الدولي لدعم النمو السياحي وتعزيز الربط الجوي للعلا

يشمل المشروع مبنى ركاب جديدًا بمساحة تقارب 30 ألف م² وبطاقة استيعابية تصل إلى 3 ملايين مسافر سنويًا، ومبنى للشحن الجوي بمساحة 5 آلاف م² يضم مرافق مخصصة للخيول والفروسية  وفق أعلى المعاييرالعالمية، ومبنى للطيران الخاص بمساحة تقارب 10 آلاف م²، ومرافق للطيران العام والمروحيات، وتمديد المدرج إلى 3 آلاف متر، إضافة إلى الطرق ومواقف السيارات ومرافق الصيانة والخدمات والوقود

كما تتوفر نحو مليون م² من الأراضي لاستخدامات تجارية مكملة، تشمل الخدمات اللوجستية والتجزئة والضيافة وخدمات الطيران

من المخطط تنفيذ المشروع بنظام البناء–النقل–التشغيل، بمدة امتياز تصل إلى 35 عامًا.

ومن المتوقع طرح طلب تقديم العروض في الربع الثالث من عام 2027، وإنجاز المشروع بحلول عام 2032.

source_rows.title: تحسين وتشغيل محطات معالجة مياه الصرف الصحي: فرصة للشراكة بين القطاع العام والخاص

raw.titleEN: Enhancement and operation of Wastewater Treatment Plants – PPP Investment Opportunity
raw.titleAR: تحسين وتشغيل محطات معالجة مياه الصرف الصحي: فرصة للشراكة بين القطاع العام والخاص
raw.descriptionEN:
In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the rehabilitation and expansion of the Wastewater Treatment Plant to increase treatment capacity, support economic growth, and enhance environmental sustainability.
The project includes the rehabilitation of the existing plant with a capacity of 8,000 m³/day and its expansion using Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (MBBR) technology in two phases, adding 18,000 m³/day in Phase I and 36,000 m³/day in Phase II, bringing the total treatment capacity to 62,000 m³/day, alongside treated wastewater storage and pumping facilities, control systems, and supporting infrastructure.
The project is planned to be delivered under a Build–Own–Operate–Transfer (BOOT) model, with a concession period of approximately 26 years, comprising 3 years of construction and rehabilitation and 23 years of operations, supported by capacity, output, and supplemental payments.
The RFP is expected to be launched in Q2 2027.
raw.descriptionAR:
تماشيًا مع خطة التخصيص المعتمدة من المركز الوطني للتخصيص، تعمل الهيئة الملكية على إعادة تأهيل وتوسعة محطة معالجة مياه الصرف الصحي لتعزيز الطاقة الاستيعابية، ودعم النمو الاقتصادي، بما يحقق الاستدامة البيئية.

يشمل المشروع إعادة تأهيل المحطة القائمة بطاقة 8,000 م³/يوميا، وتوسعتها باستخدام تقنية المفاعل الحيوي ذي الحشوات المتحركة على مرحلتين، بطاقة 18,000 م³/يومياً للمرحلة الأولى، و36,000 م³/يومياً للمرحلة الثانية، لتصل الطاقة الإجمالية إلى 62,000 م³/يومياً ، بالإضافة إلى مرافق تخزين وضخ المياه المعالجة، وأنظمة التحكم والمرافق الداعمة.
من المخطط تنفيذ المشروع وفق نموذج البناء والتملك والتشغيل ونقل الملكية ، بمدة امتياز تبلغ نحو 26 عامًا، تشمل 3 سنوات للإنشاء وإعادة التأهيل و23 عامًا للتشغيل، وبآلية مدفوعات قائمة على الطاقة الاستيعابية والإنتاج ومدفوعات تكميلية.
من المتوقع طرح طلب تقديم العروض في الربع الثاني من عام 2027.

The project includes the rehabilitation of the existing plant with a capacity of 8,000 m³/day and its expansion using Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (MBBR) technology in two phases, adding 18,000 m³/day in Phase I and 36,000 m³/day in Phase II, bringing the total treatment capacity to 62,000 m³/day, alongside treated wastewater storage and pumping facilities, control systems, and supporting infrastructure.
The project is planned to be delivered under a Build–Own–Operate–Transfer (BOOT) model, with a concession period of approximately 26 years, comprising 3 years of construction and rehabilitation and 23 years of operations, supported by capacity, output, and supplemental payments.
The RFP is expected to be launched in Q2 2027.

source_rows.title: تطوير وتشغيل وإدارة النفايات الصلبة: فرصة للشراكة بين القطاع العام والخاص

raw.titleEN: Development and Operation of a Solid Waste Management System – PPP Investment Opportunity
raw.titleAR: تطوير وتشغيل وإدارة النفايات الصلبة: فرصة للشراكة بين القطاع العام والخاص
raw.descriptionEN:
In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of an integrated solid waste management system in AlUla to enhance environmental sustainability, increase recycling rates, and support a sustainable economy.
The project includes the development of a Resource Management Park and a waste transfer station with a capacity of 76,000 tonnes annually, recycling facilities with a capacity of 45,000 tonnes annually, organic waste treatment facilities, construction and demolition waste processing facilities with a capacity of 220,000 tonnes annually, and engineered landfill cells with a total capacity of 5 million cubic metres, alongside supporting infrastructure.
The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with a concession period of 30 years, comprising 3 years of construction and 27 years of operations, supported by performance-based payments and waste gate and transfer fees.
The RFP is planned to be launched in Q2 2027.
raw.descriptionAR:
تماشيًا مع خطة التخصيص المعتمدة من المركز الوطني للتخصيص، تعمل الهيئة الملكية على تطوير منظومة متكاملة لإدارة النفايات الصلبة في العُلا، بهدف تعزيز الاستدامة البيئية، وزيادة معدلات إعادة التدوير، ودعم الاقتصاد المستدام 
يشمل المشروع تطوير مجمع لإدارة المواد ومحطة لنقل النفايات بطاقة 76 ألف طن سنويًا، ومرافق لإعادة التدوير بطاقة 45 ألف طن سنويًا، ومعالجة النفايات العضوية، ومخلفات البناء والهدم بطاقة 220 ألف طن سنويًا، إلى جانب خلايا ردم هندسية بسعة 5 ملايين متر مكعب، والمرافق الداعمة.

من المخطط طرح طلب تقديم العروض في الربع الثاني من عام 2027.

raw.titleEN: Development and Operation of Strategic Water Storage Tanks – PPP Investment Opportunity
raw.titleAR: تطوير وتشغيل الخزن الاستراتيجي للمياه: فرصة للشراكة بين القطاع العام والخاص
raw.descriptionEN:
In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of a strategic potable water storage system to ensure reliable and sustainable water supply and support AlUla’s economic and tourism growth and future development needs.
The project includes the development and operation of five strategic water storage tanks with a combined capacity of 295,000 m³, providing approximately 3 to 4 days of potable water reserves, alongside pumping stations, connection networks, and supporting infrastructure serving urban districts, heritage sites, the airport, and new development areas.
The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with a concession period of approximately 15 years, comprising 2 to 3 years of construction and 12 to 13 years of operations and maintenance, supported by availability-based payments linked to performance and water quality.
The RFP is expected to be launched in Q4 2027, with phased completion targeted by 2031.
raw.descriptionAR:
تماشيًا مع خطة التخصيص المعتمدة من المركز الوطني للتخصيص، تعمل الهيئة الملكية على تطوير منظومة استراتيجية لتخزين مياه الشرب، بهدف ضمان استدامة وموثوقية إمدادات المياه، ودعم النمو الاقتصادي والسياحي والاحتياجات المستقبلية للمحافظة.
يشمل المشروع إنشاء وتشغيل خمسة خزانات استراتيجية بسعة إجمالية تبلغ 295,000 م³، بما يوفر احتياطيًا من مياه الشرب يكفي لنحو 3 إلى 4 أيام، بالإضافة إلى محطات الضخ وشبكات الربط والمرافق الداعمة، لخدمة المناطق الحضرية والمواقع التراثية والمطار ومناطق التطوير الجديدة.من المخطط تنفيذ المشروع وفق نموذج التصميم والبناء والتمويل والتشغيل والصيانة، بمدة امتياز تبلغ نحو 15 عامًا، تشمل 2 إلى 3 سنوات للإنشاء و12 إلى 13 عامًا للتشغيل والصيانة، وبآلية مدفوعات قائمة على الإتاحة والأداء وجودة المياه.
من المتوقع طرح طلب تقديم العروض في الربع الرابع من عام 2027، على أن يتم إنجاز المشروع على مراحل حتى عام 2031.

source_rows.title: توسعة الطرق الفرعية : فرصة استثمارية للشراكة بين القطاعين العام والخاص

raw.titleEN: Expansion of Secondary Roads– PPP Investment Opportunity
raw.titleAR: توسعة الطرق الفرعية : فرصة استثمارية للشراكة بين القطاعين العام والخاص
raw.descriptionEN:
In alignment with the Privatization Plan approved by the National Center for Privatization, the Royal Commission for AlUla is advancing the development of the secondary road network to enhance connectivity, support economic and tourism growth in AlUla, and facilitate access to new development areas, heritage sites, and nature reserves.
The project covers the development of 18 secondary road and utility corridors totalling approximately 1,400 km, including new road construction and integrated infrastructure for water supply, electricity, telecommunications, street lighting, and stormwater drainage.
The project is planned to be delivered under a Design–Build–Finance–Operate–Maintain (DBFOM) model, with an availability-based payment mechanism and a concession period of approximately 20 years. Operations and maintenance will cover roads only, with utilities handed over to the relevant entities.
The RFP process for the project packages is planned to commence in early 2028, with phased completion targeted by 2033.
raw.descriptionAR:
تماشيًا مع خطة التخصيص المعتمدة من المركز الوطني للتخصيص، تعمل الهيئة الملكية على تطوير شبكة الطرق الثانوية بهدف تعزيز الربط ودعم النمو الاقتصادي والسياحي العلا. وتسهيل الوصول إلى مناطق التطوير الجديدة والمواقع التراثية والمحميات الطبيعية.
يشمل المشروع تطوير 18 مسارًا للطرق الثانوية وشبكات المرافق والخدمات، بإجمالي أطوال يبلغ نحو 1,400 كيلومتر، بما في ذلك إنشاء طرق جديدة وتطوير البنية التحتية المتكاملة لشبكات المياه والكهرباء والاتصالات وإنارة الطرق وتصريف مياه الأمطار.
من المخطط تنفيذ المشروع وفق نموذج التصميم والبناء والتمويل والتشغيل والصيانة بآلية مدفوعات قائمة على الإتاحة، ومدة امتياز تبلغ نحو 20 عامًا. ويقتصر نطاق التشغيل والصيانة على الطرق فقط، على أن تُسلّم شبكات المرافق والخدمات إلى الجهات المختصة.
من المخطط البدء في طرح طلبات تقديم العروض للحزم في بداية 2028، على أن يتم إنجاز المشروع على مراحل حتى 2033

raw.title: MEDINAH CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION WASTE TREATMENT FACILITY 4
raw.description:
The project is aiming to establish a fixed facility for construction and demolition waste (CDW) treatment, offering services in Medina
 

The global construction and demolition waste 
management market size was $115 billion in 2020. 
The market is expected to reach $542.7 billion in 
2028, with a CAGR of 5.1%

Construction and demolition waste accounts for 30% 
of the total waste produced worldwide and is 
expected to grow at a rate of 3.2 billion tons per year 
until 2025

The opportunity relies on a constant inflow of construction and 
demolition coming from private CDW collectors

Medina's population growth and expansion are the 
main drivers of construction and demolition waste 
generation

The increase in personal income and government 
incentives for homeownership

The Vision 2030 initiative includes the development 
of the infrastructure sector, which is expected to 
lead to an increase in waste generation 
necessitating further waste management solutions
* CAGR
M USD 

Due to continued growth in KSAs construction sector the 
project is looking to deliver greenfield opportunity in the sector 
with limited existing competition

The project is aligned with the KSA vision 2030 and has 
significant support within the Kingdom

Project is expected to have a stable supply of input material 
and a strong investment returns relative to peers in other 
geographies due to high number of construction projects 
expected in the Kingdom

Expected Investment size: 5.33M USD*

Plant capacity: 600,000 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.3% 

Payback period: 6-8 years

GDP Impact: 162M USD


raw.title: Local Manufacturing of Lenses

details.description: Establish local manufacturing of optical lenses—including spectacle lenses (glass and other materials)—to meet increasing demand across hospitals, clinics, and optical retailers. This opportunity aims to support both surgical and non-surgical vision care.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Increase accessibility to vision correction products and reduce dependency on imports.
• Strengthen supply chain resilience for high-volume eye care products.
• Enable modular use across hospitals, clinics, and retail markets.
• Support development of a domestic vision care ecosystem with potential for exports.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: • Growing incidence of myopia, cataracts, and presbyopia. • Rising demand for cosmetic and specialty lenses (e.g., astigmatism, keratoconus). • Push to localize high-volume consumer health products in Saudi Arabia.

raw.title: TABUK END OF LIFE VEHICLES TREATMENT
raw.description:
The aim of this opportunity is to create a waste vehicles treatment facility for the entire Tabuk cluster.

Global automobile sales began to recover from their pandemic 
drop, reaching 66.7 M units sold in 2021. It is expected to 
decline in 2022, with a 2023 still below 2019

The operation would require a stable input of end-of-life 
vehicles from producers for processing and transfer along the 
further waste treatment value chain

The rise in personal wealth and transforming 
consumer behavior in the Kingdom (increasing 
digitization, increasing personal consumption etc.) 
are increasing vehicle consumption requiring uplift 
in waste treatment solutions 

Waste management sector transformation driven 
by the Vision 2030 and initiatives to increase 
private sector participation require innovative, and 
sustainable solutions in KSA

The high level of economic and population growth in the KSA 
is expected to generate significant increase in consumption 
over the coming years, thus creating an opportunity for an 
end-of-life vehicle treatment facility operator to enter an 
attractive market

The Kingdom is placing a significant focus on the waste 
management sector as part of the Vision 2030 and the project 
can expect high level of engagement from the relevant 
authorities

raw.title: Equestrian Training Academy in Public Schools – Riyadh
raw.description: This opportunity sets up an Equestrian Training Academy inside public schools in the Riyadh region. It will build and run riding arenas, stables, and training programs for 250–400 trainees each year. Location: Al Iskan district, Riyadh city, on a site of more than 12,000 m², using land and buildings already provided by the Ministry of Education. It is the first academy of its kind inside a public school, helping promote horse riding as part of Saudi heritage.

source_rows.title: Terminal Operating System (ToS) associated services

raw.title: Terminal Operating System (ToS) associated services

details.description:
Localize ToS associated services.

ToS associated services may include:
- Database administration services which involve the management, maintenance, and optimization of databases by a team of experts.
- ToS support services which include technical support for ToS systems and software updates.

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Associated services are outsourced to global players today.
• Potential to expand these services to GCC port operators, since ToS systems deployed in the region are similar to the ones in Saudi Arabia (e.g., Abu Dhabi ports – Master Terminal ToS; Mwani – Navis N4 ToS).

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - Saudi Arabia to increase port throughput from 9M TEU to 40M TEU by 2030, which results in increased need for ToS associated services to improve efficiency, resulting in higher spend on these services. - Future digitization efforts (i.e., smart ports) are expected to drive data traffic volume growth by ca 26% per annum. - Regional demand growth due to upcoming projects (e.g., Kuwait port expansion).

source_rows.title: HAIL HAZARDOUS INDUSTRIAL WASTE TREATMENT

raw.title: HAIL HAZARDOUS INDUSTRIAL WASTE TREATMENT
raw.description:
The project aims to establish a treatment center mainly for hazardous industrial waste across Hail Cluster.

The global industrial waste management market was valued at USD 
791.14B in 2020. It is estimated to expand at a CAGR of 10.4% from 
2021 to 2031 

The global industrial waste management market is expected to cross the 
value of USD 2.3 T by the end of 2031

Industrial waste constitutes approximately half of the share of the overall 
waste generated across the globe

The operation would mainly require a continuous input of hazardous 
industrial waste from private waste collectors. This opportunity also 
receives waste from other streams such as agricultural, healthcare 
and ELV waste.
The historic and projected growth in industrial sector as 
part of the KSA transformation requires innovative solutions 
for treatment of hazardous industrial waste
The drive to increase private sector participation and 
competitiveness in the economy are further drivers for 
formulation of the opportunity
The need to modernize waste management sector in the 
Kingdom is a key driver to attracting investors and 
operators 
* CAGR
M USD 

As KSA continues to expand the industrial sector as part of Vision 2030 
the project enables a hazardous industrial waste operator to capitalize 
on a growing segment on Saudi Arabia's economy

The opportunity allows a potential investor to deliver a greenfield project 
with no constraints from legacy infrastructure in a developing sector 
enabling a full use of best-in-class operational and technical solutions

Expected Investment size: 18M USD*

Plant capacity: 16,423 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 7.63 years

GDP Impact: 105M USD


Service provision is characterized by limited service coverage, given

•
Environmental services sector in KSA is at nascent stage; as such, end-
use sectors, environmental service providers, and governmental 
entities are likely to require environmental capability building services
•
Expected Investment size of SAR ~ 6 Million
•
Expected IRR: ~ 23% for the 10-year IRR
•
Payback period: 5.7 years
•
Location: Central region, Western region, and Eastern region
•
Capability building market is in its developing stage, with rapidly 
growing demand (13% YoY) presenting an opportunity for new entrants
•
Only two entities are licensed to provide capability building services 
with a very limited selection of topics, which presents a significant 
demand-supply gap
•
NCEC is targeting a 9x increase in registered entities with 
an environmental impact, requiring capability building to 
enhance their compliance
•
As service providers expand their service offerings to 
meet increasing demand, they seek specialized 
environmental training and upskilling from specialized 
providers
•
Listed entities are increasingly disclosing environmental 
performance, leading to growing demand for 
environmental capability-building services
•
Global market for environmental capability building services is 
experiencing significant growth, driven by increasing environmental 
awareness, stringent regulations, and the need for sustainable business 
practices
•
Market is serviced by a range of providers, including multinational 
consulting firms, specialized environmental consultancies, and industry-
specific experts
•
Strong focus on integrating digital solutions like e-learning and virtual 
training, and on building skills for technological adaptation, especially 
in environmental monitoring

details.description:
- Description: An opportunity exists to establish local manufacturing plant with a capacity of 70 ktpa for the refractory materials to capitalize on the increasing upcoming demand in Saudi Arabia.

- Application: Refractory equipment, pivotal in the mining sector, encompasses specialized tools for producing, installing, and upkeeping refractory materials essential for industrial operations.

- Products / Services Targeted: Equipment MRO Refractory (Bricks, Castables, Monolithics).

strategicBenefitsPoints.point: • Demand for the refractory materials will be mainly driven by recovery in the construction, infrastructure industrial, and mining sectors.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - Refractory Saudi demand in 2020 was 160-170 ktpa, growing at 6-7% CAGR until 2027. - Significant growth expected in the global market as well as in Saudi Arabia in the years to come. - Similar growth observed in neighboring countries, thus opening the filtration market beyond Saudi Arabia.

source_rows.title: YANBU END OF LIFE VEHICLES TREATMENT FACILITY

raw.title: YANBU END OF LIFE VEHICLES TREATMENT FACILITY
raw.description:
The aim of this opportunity is to create a waste vehicles treatment facility for the entire Yanbu cluster.

Global automobile sales began to recover from their pandemic 
drop, reaching 66.7 M units sold in 2021. It is expected to 
decline in 2022, with a 2023 still below 2019

The operation would require a stable input of end-of-life 
vehicles from producers for processing and transfer along the 
further waste treatment value chain

The rise in personal wealth and transforming 
consumer behavior in the Kingdom (increasing 
digitization, increasing personal consumption etc.) 
are increasing vehicle consumption requiring uplift 
in waste treatment solutions 

Waste management sector transformation driven 
by the Vision 2030 and initiatives to increase 
private sector participation require innovative, and 
sustainable solutions in KSA

The high level of economic and population growth in the KSA 
is expected to generate significant increase in consumption 
over the coming years, thus creating an opportunity for an 
end-of-life vehicle treatment facility operator to enter an 
attractive market

The Kingdom is placing a significant focus on the waste 
management sector as part of the Vision 2030 and the project 
can expect high level of engagement from the relevant 
authorities 
* CAGR
M USD 

Expected Investment size: 3M USD*

Plant capacity: 8,500 tons of waste per year

Expected IRR: 10.30%

Payback period: 8.35 years

GDP Impact: 39M USD

Location (Region): Yanbu Cluster

source_rows.title: Alloys

raw.title: Alloys

details.description:
- Description: Significant opportunity exists to establish local capacity of 7500 (MTPA) minimum. 

Saudi Arabia can leverage its strategic location and strong logistics infrastructure to enhance export capability.

- Saudi Arabia has an opportunity for first mover advantage due to non-existent local production of alloys and alloy-based parts

- Products / Services Targeted: Raw Materials and Chemicals (Alloys)

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Saudi Arabia has the world’s largest integrated Aluminum city at Ras Al-Khair which provides easy & uninterrupted access of feedstock.
• Saudi Arabia is strategically located at the crossroads of several markets that have good demand potential.
• Saudi Arabia benefits from having abundant and easy access to utilities, raw materials and a world class infrastructure with good access to port.
• Progressive value chain integration will position Aluminum master alloys as an attractive niche product offering value addition potential locally, with high export opportunities and higher netback realization.

keyGrowthDrivers.title: Key Growth Drivers
keyGrowthDrivers.description: - Titanium alloys: Global Titanium Alloy Market Was Valued at US$4.3B in 2021 and is Projected to Reach US$8.4B by the End of 2029, Exhibiting a healthy CAGR of 6.5% Between 2022 and 2029. - Manganese-based alloys: Global growth at a rate of 4.7% in the forecast period 2022 to 2029.

source_rows.title: Bearings, Bushings and Wheels

raw.title: Bearings, Bushings and Wheels

details.description:
- Description: An opportunity exists in building strength in local capability and capacity for bearings, also for bushings, wheels, and related-parts.

- Application: Vital in mining, bearings, bushings, and wheels are mechanical essentials, enabling diverse functions by facilitating smooth movement, reducing friction, and supporting heavy loads. 

- Products / Services Targeted: Equipment MRO (Roller Bearings, Ball Bearings, Drill Jig Bushings, Steel Shoulder, Bushings).

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• The global market size for bearings is estimated at USD 48B for 2021, increasing to USD 56B by 2026 (CAGR of 3.4% during period).
• In Saudi Arabia, local demand is supplied via imports, while global firms import and distribute in Saudi Arabia. This prompts a chance for local production to replace imports.
• Saudi Arabia demand for Bearings, Bushings, & Wheels is met through imports with 84% of this demand originating from high-cost countries

source_rows.title: Data center power equipment

raw.title: Data center power equipment

details.description:
- Description: Provide power equipment to the 1,100 MW anticipated data center capacity that ensures consistent, reliable and uninterrupted power supply.

- Service: Assembly, installation, and after sales services of data center power equipment in Saudi Arabia including but not limited to uninterruptible power supply (UPS), back up generators, power distribution units (PDU), electrical switchgear, automatic transfer switch (ATS), and static transfer switch (STS).

- Customers: Potential key clients include PIF Portfolio Companies, global data center services players attracted to Saudi Arabia, hyperscalers, tech players entering/ increasing share in data center sector (e.g., Huawei).

strategicBenefitsPoints.point:
• Skyrocketing data storage needs from personal data protection law and cloud computing Regulatory Framework.
• Growing need for data center supply from government bodies and corporates driven by digitalization trend and smart government initiatives.
